product.name: LocalCloud
product.productionBoundary: LocalCloud emulates bounded local development workflows. Validate application behavior against real Google Cloud before production deployment.

runtimeImage.limitation: The repository agrees across the reviewed runtime launcher and CLI, but the mutable latest tag has no qualified assembled-image digest.

operator.manualDockerCommand:
docker volume create localcloud-data

docker run -d --name localcloud \
  -p 127.0.0.1:5380-5405:5380-5405 \
  -m 4g \
  -v localcloud-data:/var/lib/localcloud \
  agentcloud/localcloud:latest

supportedHosts: Linux with glibc 2.35+ on arm64 or amd64
cli.integrity: The installer verifies SHA-256 checksums, exact archive members, and the executable semantic version. Release automation separately publishes Sigstore bundles; install.sh does not verify them.
cli.releaseBoundary: CLI behavior is documented for version 0.1.13 from revision 398299d445e89329744080c81a179a03c7763daf. Use localcloud --version to confirm the installed release.

acceptedEnvelopes.description: Top-level service keys for the default project.
A services mapping for one selected project.
A projects mapping whose entries each contain service seed data.

limitations: Seed sections create sample resources; they do not establish supported application integrations. Consult operation-level compatibility.

Each seed or import answer reports every section as applied, unsupported, skipped_disabled or unknown_service with its record count. A seed that cannot be applied answers 400 or 500, and a malformed seed is refused before anything is written.
POST /reseed removes only the resources the seed wrote and applies the samples again; a global reseed requires confirm=true. Cloud Run, GKE and Compute samples are stopped and recreated.
server.auto_seed: false (LOCALCLOUD_AUTO_SEED=false) or LOCALCLOUD_TERRAFORM_MODE=true skips the automatic seed at startup.
Service Usage has no seed section. The runtime has no volatile seed mode.
Managed CLI lifecycle commands do not mount or apply seed files; host.seed is accepted but ignored. Container bootstrap and Console reseeding own samples.

terraform.credentialRequirement: A syntactically valid fake service-account JSON file; /dev/null is not sufficient for provider v7.

networkModes.description: Use generated custom endpoints for resources whose provider clients honor them.
requirements: eval generated values from /env?format=terraform or localcloud env --format terraform

networkModes.description: Use LocalCloud DNS/HTTP/HTTPS routing for clients that ignore custom endpoints.

limitations: Some resources require transparent DNS/HTTPS routing and a trusted LocalCloud certificate.
BigQuery ignores its custom endpoint and requires transparent routing.
Resource support is bounded to maintained qualification evidence.

runtimeTelemetry.identifier: Pseudonymous installation identifier kept by the CLI
events: CLI startup errors as scrubbed one-line signatures
hourly CLI heartbeat: CLI version, platform, configured services and command counts
limitations: The runtime image sends no usage telemetry and does not read LOCALCLOUD_TELEMETRY; the Console sends no analytics.

The LocalCloud CLI sends its reports from start, restart, reset and stop; LOCALCLOUD_TELEMETRY=false or DO_NOT_TRACK in the CLI's environment stops them. Undelivered events are retried on a later run.

outboundBehaviors.control: The Console looks up newer image tags only when the viewer turns the update check on; the lookup sends the image name and tag.
Pub/Sub push endpoints, Cloud Tasks and Cloud Scheduler HTTP targets, Cloud Functions and Workflows calls go where you point them. Pub/Sub push to metadata-server addresses is refused.
The gcp-live IAM mode never contacts Google; it refuses bearer tokens it cannot verify and fails closed.
No license key is enforced, so the runtime never contacts a license service.

events: sampled browser web vitals and website release

limitations: Core operation can continue offline after the image is present only when outbound features are disabled or unused; do not describe the product as categorically offline.

services.name: Cloud Storage

persistence.backingStore: Filesystem at /var/lib/localcloud/gcs-data (objects, generations, bucket settings, HMAC keys, notification configurations and undelivered notifications); bucket ownership and gateway bucket IAM policies in the bundled PostgreSQL
persistence.restartBehavior: Survives process and container restarts while the LocalCloud volume is retained. Each write, overwrite, delete, restore and move is journaled, so a restart after a crash completes or undoes it, and undelivered notifications are sent after the restart.
recoveryLimitations: No production durability or replication semantics.
Project exports and checkpoints hold only bucket names, locations, versioning settings and live object contents; restore the rest from the volume itself.

limitations: The gateway owns the Storage ports: 5382 (plaintext), 5392 (TLS, when TLS is enabled) and the /storage routes of 5380 and 5381. Each applies the browser policy, so a browser request from an origin that server.allowed_origins does not admit is refused before it reaches Storage. SDKs, gsutil, gcloud and Terraform send no browser headers and are not affected.

Bucket IAM policies that LocalCloud's IAM checks read are managed through the /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/iam routes on 5380 (TLS 5381). The same calls sent to 5382 are answered by the Storage engine's own policy store, which strict mode does not read.

IAM modes: open allows every Storage request, and permissive evaluates without refusing. Strict decides each bucket and object request on project and bucket policies for the verified caller: a LocalCloud-signed token, or the X-LocalCloud-User header when the request carries no credential. Unsigned bearer strings and forged tokens are refused with 403. gcp-live refuses Storage requests (401 without a bearer token, 403 with one), because this build never contacts Google.

Managed-folder IAM policies are stored and returned, but strict-mode decisions use project and bucket policies. Organization and folder inheritance, deny policies, custom role definitions and conditions on project bindings are not modeled.
Lifecycle rules (Delete, SetStorageClass, AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload) are stored and returned, but LocalCloud does not run them on a schedule, so objects are not deleted or reclassified by age.
New buckets have soft delete turned off unless a policy is set, where Cloud Storage defaults to 7 days. objects.bulkRestore is not served; restore soft-deleted objects one at a time.

Bucket locations are validated against Google's location list and checked against Cloud KMS key locations, but data is not placed geographically. ipFilter is stored and reported but requests are not filtered. Global bucket-name uniqueness and domain-ownership verification are not checked.

Customer-managed encryption uses LocalCloud's Cloud KMS keys: object data is encrypted with a data key that the Cloud KMS key wraps, and a disabled or unknown key is refused. In strict mode, grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key to service-storage@<project>.localcloud.internal. A denied key permission answers 403 forbidden. Customer-supplied keys sent over plain HTTP are not refused.

Notifications publish to local Pub/Sub topics at least once, so a message can arrive twice, and ordering is not guaranteed. The topic must exist when the notification is created; with gcloud, create the topic first and pass --skip-topic-setup. Failed publications retry with a capped backoff, and a configuration that keeps failing for 7 days is deleted.

RSA V4 signed URLs are accepted without signature verification, because LocalCloud configures no signer keys; V2 RSA signed URLs are refused. HMAC-signed V2 and V4 requests, URLs and form policies are verified on the XML routes.

HMAC keys are created for a service-account email in the project; whether that account exists in LocalCloud IAM is not checked. Path-style XML requests work on localhost and loopback addresses, and virtual-hosted requests use the host name localhost on any port. A signed Host header must not be rewritten after signing.
The Storage v2 gRPC API is not served on LocalCloud's Storage ports; use the JSON or XML API.
Filesystem storage refuses object names that end in .metadata and names whose last segment is .fake-gcs-folder.

Project exports and checkpoints carry each bucket's name, location and versioning setting and each live object's bytes and content type. Other bucket and object metadata, bucket IAM policies and noncurrent generations are not restored from them. A project reset deletes every generation before it deletes the bucket, removes the bucket's IAM policy, and reports a bucket it cannot clear as partial_failure.
LocalCloud's own Storage calls (seed, reset, checkpoints, Firestore export and import) use an internal credential, so strict and gcp-live policies do not block them.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: buckets.create/list/delete
limitations: Bucket insert, get, list (filtered by project), patch, update (PUT) and delete keep the full bucket resource: labels, versioning, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention, CORS, retention policy and lock, soft delete, lifecycle, hierarchical namespace, default encryption key and metageneration preconditions. Locations are validated and stored without physical placement. Deleting a bucket that holds live objects answers 412, where Cloud Storage answers 409.

operations.label: objects.upload/download/list/delete
limitations: Media, multipart, form, resumable and XML API multipart uploads; ranged downloads; listing with prefixes, delimiters, generations and paging; rewrite, copy, compose and atomic objects.move; generation and metageneration preconditions; MD5 and CRC32C validation; JSON batch requests. Response links and resumable-upload locations name the address the client called.

operations.label: buckets.getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy/testIamPermissions
limitations: On 5380 (TLS 5381) the policy routes use LocalCloud's project-owned policy store, with etags, role and member validation, and conditions on version 3 policies. In strict mode testIamPermissions returns the caller's granted permissions; open and permissive return the requested ones. gcp-live answers 401 without a bearer token and 403 with one, and refuses policy writes with 405. Calls sent to 5382 reach the Storage engine's own policy store instead.

operations.label: mode-aware object data-plane authorization
limitations: Every bucket and object request on 5382, 5392 and the gateway's /storage routes is authorized by LocalCloud's IAM mode. Open allows it, permissive evaluates without refusing, and strict checks the Storage permission (including multipart upload, folder and managed-folder permissions) against project and bucket policies for the verified caller, refusing with 403. HMAC-signed requests act as the key's service account. gcp-live refuses Storage requests. Managed-folder policies are not used in these decisions.

operations.label: notificationConfigs.create/list/delete and Pub/Sub event delivery
limitations: Notification configurations (up to 10 per event type and 100 per bucket) deliver OBJECT_FINALIZE, OBJECT_METADATA_UPDATE, OBJECT_DELETE and OBJECT_ARCHIVE events to local Pub/Sub topics, filtered by event type and object-name prefix, with JSON_API_V1 or NONE payloads and custom attributes. Uploads, metadata changes, deletes, moves and versioned overwrites raise events. The topic must exist at creation. Delivery is at least once, failed publications retry from a persistent queue, and configurations and undelivered messages survive restart.

operations.label: HMAC key management and XML signature authentication
limitations: Key create, list (filtered by service account, paged, optionally with deleted keys), get, update with etag and delete of inactive keys, at most ten keys per service account, and the secret returned only on creation. Google and AWS V2 and V4 signatures are verified in headers, signed URLs and form policies, with a 15-minute request window. In strict mode a signed request acts as the key's service account.

operations.label: Object Lifecycle Management and retention enforcement
limitations: Bucket retention policies (and their lock), object retention, temporary holds, event-based holds and default event-based holds are enforced: they block delete, overwrite and move until they expire or are released. Lifecycle rules are stored and returned but LocalCloud does not run them on a schedule, so they never delete or reclassify objects by age.

operations.label: managed folders
limitations: Managed folders support insert, get, list (prefix and paging), delete (with allowNonEmpty) and getIamPolicy, setIamPolicy and testIamPermissions. Hierarchical-namespace folders support insert, get, list, delete and rename. Managed-folder policies are stored and returned, but LocalCloud's strict mode decides on project and bucket policies.

operations.label: persistent bucket versioning and OBJECT_ARCHIVE notifications
limitations: With versioning.enabled, replacing, deleting or moving a live object keeps it as a noncurrent generation that survives restart. versions=true lists every generation, get, download, copy and rewrite take a generation, and deleting a generation by number is permanent. A bucket that still holds noncurrent generations is not deleted (409). Overwrites, deletes and moves in a versioned bucket raise OBJECT_ARCHIVE notifications.

operations.label: customer-managed (Cloud KMS) and customer-supplied encryption keys
limitations: Object data is encrypted at rest with customer-supplied AES-256 keys, with a key named on the request, or with a bucket's default Cloud KMS key, on the JSON, XML, form and multipart paths. Cloud KMS keys are LocalCloud's own, must match the bucket location, and a disabled or unknown key is refused. In strict mode the key needs roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter for service-storage@<project>.localcloud.internal.

operations.label: soft delete and bucket/object restore
limitations: A soft-delete policy (0, or 7 to 90 days) keeps deleted objects and buckets restorable; objects.restore creates a new live generation and buckets.restore brings a bucket back by generation. New buckets have soft delete off where Cloud Storage defaults to 7 days, and objects.bulkRestore is not served.

services.name: Pub/Sub

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (topics, subscriptions, snapshots, schemas, messages and delivery state); retained messages are also held in memory
persistence.restartBehavior: Topics, subscriptions, snapshots, schemas and unacknowledged messages are reloaded at start with their original message IDs and publish times; message IDs are never reissued. A message leased before the restart is offered again once its ack deadline passes. Push delivery and StreamingPull streams restart, so clients reconnect.
recoveryLimitations: Delivery is at least once: a push or acknowledgement whose result is not stored can be redelivered.
A database that cannot be read in full is refused rather than loaded partially: Pub/Sub stays unavailable until it is repaired and LocalCloud restarts.
A mounted volume gives no production replication, durability or disaster-recovery guarantees.

limitations: enableExactlyOnceDelivery is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED (HTTP 501). Export subscriptions (bigqueryConfig, cloudStorageConfig), message transforms, topic ingestionDataSourceSettings and topic messageStoragePolicy are not applied: a request that sets them succeeds, the field is dropped and reads do not return it. Topic kmsKeyName is stored and returned but encrypts nothing. DetachSubscription answers UNIMPLEMENTED.

enableMessageOrdering is stored and returned, and orderingKey travels with each message through pull, StreamingPull and push, but delivery does not hold back later messages of a key while an earlier one is outstanding or being redelivered. Do not rely on per-key ordering locally.

By default no message expires by age (pubsub setting enforce_subscription_retention: false). Unacknowledged messages, and acknowledged ones a subscription retains, stay until they are acknowledged, purged or their subscription is deleted, whatever messageRetentionDuration the subscription names; the resource still reports the value it was given. With enforce_subscription_retention: true a message expires after its subscription's messageRetentionDuration, or after subscription_retention_days (default 7, at most 31) when the subscription names none. Changes apply at the next start.

Retained messages are held in memory and reloaded from PostgreSQL at start, so a backlog that is never consumed grows memory and startup time. Purge test subscriptions or turn retention enforcement on.

Subscription expirationPolicy is stored and returned without validation and is never enforced, so no subscription expires locally. A subscription created without one returns none, where Google returns a 31-day default.

Deleting a topic keeps its subscriptions, shown with topic _deleted-topic_, and their backlog, also across a restart. The topic name can be reused at once and a recreated topic starts empty; new publishes reach only subscriptions created on the new topic.

A push succeeds on HTTP 102, 200, 201, 202 or 204. Any other answer, a connection failure or a 10-second timeout is a NACK that follows the subscription's retry and dead-letter policies. Pushes to cloud metadata-server addresses (metadata.google.internal, 169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254 and names that resolve to them) are refused and NACKed with no token minted; loopback, LAN and other link-local targets work. Push ignores proxy environment variables.

Authenticated push ID tokens are signed by the LocalCloud issuer (/identity/status, keys at /oauth2/v3/certs), not https://accounts.google.com, so receivers must trust the local JWKS. Setting oidcToken checks no iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission in any IAM mode, and the Pub/Sub service agent's token-creator role is not modeled.

Topic and subscription IAM policies (getIamPolicy, setIamPolicy, testIamPermissions) are stored by the local IAM service, but no Pub/Sub call evaluates them. In strict mode the gateway checks the caller's verified LocalCloud credential against its access-policy rules for REST and gRPC calls on the gateway and on the dedicated port 5383 (PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST); open and permissive modes admit every call.

Schemas must be self-contained: an Avro definition, or one top-level proto2 or proto3 message without imports or services. Protobuf definitions are checked with protoc in the image; when it cannot run, schema checks and publishes to schema topics answer UNAVAILABLE (HTTP 503).

Seeds, GET /export and project checkpoints carry each topic and subscription as its full REST resource (a format_version 2 section); a checkpoint section in the older name-only form is refused. Messages, snapshots, schema definitions and Cloud Functions trigger bindings are not captured, a subscription on _deleted-topic_ is left out, and a replace restore refuses a topic that uses a schema (FAILED_PRECONDITION) before it clears anything. A seed creates only what is absent.

A storage failure answers INTERNAL (REST 500) instead of succeeding. If the saved Pub/Sub state cannot be loaded at start, every Pub/Sub call answers INTERNAL until the database is repaired and LocalCloud restarts, and /health reports state_not_loaded.
Retry dispatch, push polling (about once a second) and retention sweeps are local schedules. They do not reproduce Google's production scale, availability, regional placement or service-agent IAM.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: topics.create/get/list/update/delete
limitations: Served over gRPC and REST on the gateway and on port 5383, with listing of a topic's subscriptions and snapshots. Updates cover labels, messageRetentionDuration (10 minutes to 31 days) and schemaSettings and are all or nothing: an unknown or immutable mask path answers 400 and changes nothing. A schema reference that does not exist is NOT_FOUND.

operations.label: subscriptions.create/get/list/update/delete/modifyPushConfig
limitations: ackDeadlineSeconds is 10 to 600, deadLetterPolicy.maxDeliveryAttempts 5 to 100, and filters cannot be changed after create. Updates are all or nothing. A deleted subscription ends its StreamingPull streams with NOT_FOUND. DetachSubscription is not implemented; enableExactlyOnceDelivery is refused and export or transform settings are dropped.

operations.label: publish/pull/ack/modifyAckDeadline
limitations: Publish (up to 1000 messages per request), Pull, StreamingPull, Acknowledge and ModifyAckDeadline (0 to 600 seconds; 0 returns the message at once). StreamingPull honours maxOutstandingMessages (default 1000) and wakes on publish. Messages without attributes carry an empty attributes map. Message IDs only increase, and publishTime keeps nanoseconds across a restart.

operations.label: subscription filters, dead-letter forwarding, retry policies
limitations: Attribute filters, dead-letter forwarding after maxDeliveryAttempts with delivery-attempt counts, and retry policies shared by pull, StreamingPull and push: after a NACK or failed push the wait starts at minimumBackoff and doubles per attempt up to maximumBackoff (default 600 seconds). A message whose dead-letter topic was deleted is delivered normally and dead-lettered once the topic exists again.

operations.label: retention, snapshot CRUD, timestamp and snapshot seek
limitations: Snapshot create, get, list, update and delete, and seek to a snapshot or a timestamp; replayed messages get new ack IDs. A snapshot expires 7 days after the oldest unacknowledged message it captures, a create that would expire within an hour is refused, and an expired snapshot's name can be reused. A timestamp seek replays only messages the subscription still holds, so set retainAckedMessages to replay acknowledged ones. Message age expiry applies only with enforce_subscription_retention on.

operations.label: schema and revision lifecycle, validation, publish enforcement
limitations: Schema create, get, list, delete, revision commit, rollback, list and delete, validateSchema and validateMessage. Avro and proto2/proto3 with JSON or binary encoding. A topic enforces its schema and revision range on publish, and an invalid message fails the whole batch. Publishing to a topic whose schema was deleted is NOT_FOUND (REST 404).

operations.label: PushConfig oidcToken on create/update/modifyPushConfig, signed push delivery
limitations: oidcToken (serviceAccountEmail, audience) is accepted on create, update and modifyPushConfig over gRPC and REST, stored and returned. Each push attempt sends Authorization: Bearer with an ID token from the LocalCloud issuer for that account, with the configured audience or, when empty, the push endpoint URL. If the account is missing or disabled, or identity is not ready, the message is not sent and follows the NACK, retry and dead-letter path; other subscriptions on the topic are unaffected. No iam.serviceAccounts.actAs check is made when the token is configured.

operations.label: push payload unwrapping (noWrapper), pubsubWrapper and the x-goog-version push attribute
limitations: The default wrapped push is a JSON envelope with subscription and message (base64 data, messageId, publishTime, attributes, orderingKey), plus deliveryAttempt when a dead-letter policy is set. noWrapper sends the message data as the body; with writeMetadata it adds the x-goog-pubsub-subscription-name, message-id, publish-time and ordering-key headers and one header per message attribute, so attribute names must be valid HTTP header names or the push fails and is retried. pushConfig.attributes defaults x-goog-version to v1, which does not change the payload; other non-x-goog entries are also sent as request headers. The settings round-trip on gRPC and REST and across a restart.

operations.label: subscription expirationPolicy and topic messageStoragePolicy
limitations: Subscription expirationPolicy is stored and returned on gRPC and REST and across a restart, without validation, and never expires a subscription. Topic messageStoragePolicy is not stored: create drops it and an update mask naming it is accepted without effect, so reads do not return it.

operations.label: exactly-once delivery, message ordering, export subscriptions and transforms
limitations: enableExactlyOnceDelivery is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED (HTTP 501). enableMessageOrdering is stored and ordering keys are carried, but per-key ordered delivery is not enforced. bigqueryConfig, cloudStorageConfig and messageTransforms are dropped without an error and have no effect.

services.name: Firestore

persistence.backingStore: Per-project write-ahead log and checkpoint files under /var/lib/localcloud/firestore; the enabled state is kept in the bundled PostgreSQL
persistence.restartBehavior: Every acknowledged write survives process and container restarts, including a crash, while the LocalCloud volume is retained. Document values and their create and update times are kept.
recoveryLimitations: Directories written by older preview builds are refused, never converted or overwritten.
Project checkpoints and exports carry the full Firestore state (every database, documents with their timestamps, Rules and index metadata); restoring one needs replace: true.
With server.persistence false, Firestore runs in memory and its state is lost when the gateway stops.

limitations: Firestore is disabled by default to save resources. Enable it with localcloud start --services firestore, or set services.catalog.firestore.defaultEnabled to true.

The default compatibility profile follows Google's Firestore emulator: composite indexes are not required, listeners resend changed results instead of incremental changes, and TTL policies, point-in-time reads, backups, managed export and import, bulk delete, Query Explain and the Rules deployment API are not available. Set compatibilityProfile: production in the Firestore service config to enable them.
Only Firestore Native mode is served. Datastore mode, the Datastore API and Enterprise edition pipelines (ExecutePipeline) are not available.

Security Rules are evaluated for Firebase and mock callers. Set rulesFile in the Firestore service config to load a default Rules file of up to 1 MiB; a change to it applies after a Firestore restart. Rules regular-expression functions cover a bounded set of patterns.

Managed exports and imports round-trip within LocalCloud only: an export written by Google cannot be imported, and LocalCloud's exports cannot be imported into Google Cloud. Exports write to local Cloud Storage.

In strict IAM mode, service-account credentials are checked against project and database IAM on every call and stream message. gcp-live refuses Firestore requests because this build never contacts Google.

Browser requests to 5384 are served only for origins the gateway's browser policy admits (loopback, the gateway's own origin and server.allowed_origins). Admitted origins get CORS headers with credentials allowed, so the Firebase JS SDK works; other origins are refused with 403, where Google accepts any origin.
CMEK databases check the state of a LocalCloud Cloud KMS key, but documents are not encrypted with it. Multi-region replication, the availability SLA and managed key custody are cloud-only.

The data directory uses format version 2 while LocalCloud is in preview. A directory from an older build is refused: Firestore stays stopped with failure_code data_directory_refused until the directory is moved or deleted.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: documents.create/read/update/delete
limitations: Document get, create, update with masks, delete with preconditions, list, batch get, atomic Commit, BatchWrite, field transforms (server timestamp, increment, array union and remove) and read-write and read-only transactions, over gRPC and REST on port 5384 and the WebChannel protocol the web SDKs use. Named databases are separate.

operations.label: queries/index behavior
limitations: Filters (equality, range, IN, array-contains, collection-group; NOT_IN and OR with some combination restrictions), ordering, cursors, aggregations and real-time listeners. Index configuration is stored in both profiles; the production profile also enforces READY composite indexes, builds them asynchronously, supports vector indexes for FindNearest and serves Query Explain.

operations.label: Security Rules evaluation and deployment
limitations: Rules are evaluated per database for Firebase and mock callers on reads, writes, queries and listeners. A default Rules file loads from the rulesFile setting. The production profile adds the Firebase Rules REST API (rulesets, releases and projects.test) for single-file sources; releases.getExecutable is not served.

operations.label: TTL, point-in-time recovery, backups, bulk delete and managed export/import
limitations: With compatibilityProfile: production: TTL field policies delete expired documents; point-in-time reads cover up to seven days of retained history; backup schedules, backups and RestoreDatabase; CloneDatabase from point-in-time snapshots; bulk delete by collection group; ExportDocuments and ImportDocuments to and from local Cloud Storage, compatible only with exports written by LocalCloud.

services.name: Bigtable

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud/pgdata (or the PostgreSQL named by LOCALCLOUD_PG_HOST and related variables)
persistence.restartBehavior: Tables, rows, views, schema bundles, backups, IAM policies, long-running operations and change-stream records survive process and container restarts while the LocalCloud volume is retained.
recoveryLimitations: No production durability or replication semantics.
A remote PostgreSQL is reached over TLS by default; a server without TLS needs LOCALCLOUD_PG_SSLMODE=disable.
Project checkpoints do not capture Bigtable; a project reset clears its Bigtable data even when the service is disabled.

limitations: IAM policies on instances, tables, views and backups are stored with etags and returned, but they are not evaluated: TestIamPermissions grants every requested permission. In strict IAM mode the gateway's port 5385 requires an identified caller and applies the strict-mode policy file to gRPC methods.
Change streams use one partition for the whole key space, so partition split and merge are not exercised.
Multi-column continuous materialized-view row keys use an encoding that has not been verified against Cloud Bigtable. HLL++ sketches use ZetaSketch v2 bytes.
Legacy table snapshot RPCs (SnapshotTable, GetSnapshot, ListSnapshots, DeleteSnapshot, CreateTableFromSnapshot), hot tablets and memory layers return Unimplemented. Use backups for data protection.

ST_REGIONSTATS is not available, and some GoogleSQL geography functions have local limits. Cluster nodes and autoscaling settings are stored without capacity effects; replication, failover and Data Boost isolation are not emulated.
In open and permissive IAM modes, project and instance IDs are accepted without creating the instance first; in strict and gcp-live modes a request that names a missing instance answers NOT_FOUND.
The REST backup listing ignores filter, orderBy and pagination and returns name, sourceTable and expireTime; the native API honors them.
Project exports and checkpoints do not capture Bigtable data; they name it under not_captured_services. Use backups to keep data.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: instances/tables/families
limitations: Instances, clusters, app profiles, tables, column families, authorized views and schema bundles are validated metadata: ID and field rules, response views, update masks, pagination, deletion protection, soft delete with 7-day undelete, initial splits and row key schemas, with a durable long-running-operation registry. gcloud and Terraform use the REST admin API on 5380, which forwards to the emulator and returns its errors. Cluster node and autoscaling settings have no capacity effect.

operations.label: row mutations and reads
limitations: Each mutation is validated before any cell is written, so a row changes atomically. MutateRows returns per-entry codes and honors idempotency tokens. Aggregate families (Sum, Min, Max, HLL++), every RowFilter including Sink and ValueBitmask, read-modify-write, SampleRowKeys within row ranges, request stats, authorized-view, materialized-view and app-profile targets, and the OpenTable session protocol are supported. ReadRows streams production-shaped chunks and progress-only last_scanned_row_key responses.

operations.label: cbt CLI compatibility
limitations: Set BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST and pass -project to cbt unless the project is set in .cbtrc or gcloud; GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT alone does not select it. Table commands also need -instance. Clear stored -admin-endpoint and -data-endpoint overrides so the emulator variable applies. In open and permissive IAM modes any project and instance ID is accepted without registration; in strict mode create the instance first.

operations.label: localcloud console data browser
limitations: The Console browses rows, writes cells and deletes rows, and manages instances, tables, app profiles, views and backups through LocalCloud's REST admin API, which forwards every call to the emulator and returns its errors with the Google HTTP mapping. Row writes validate every cell first and never create a table; adding an existing row key answers 409. Binary cell values are returned base64. The Console SQL editor uses LocalCloud's own translator.

operations.label: data survives emulator restart
limitations: All resource state, including table policies, views, schema bundles, backups and their rows, IAM policies, long-running operations, the change-stream outbox and idempotency tokens, persists in PostgreSQL in the LocalCloud volume.

operations.label: materialized views (CMVs)
limitations: Continuous materialized views are built from GoogleSQL GROUP BY or ORDER BY queries over existing tables, are read-only and deletion protected, and are recomputed before a read when stale. They are read through materialized_view_name or GoogleSQL, and their query cannot be changed. Local query restrictions and the aggregate allowlist differ from Cloud Bigtable, and multi-column row keys use a local encoding.

operations.label: GoogleSQL queries and logical views
limitations: PrepareQuery and ExecuteQuery run GoogleSQL locally; a schema change returns FailedPrecondition (PREPARED_QUERY_EXPIRED). Logical views are queryable, including parameterized views that read VIEW_PARAMETERS. ST_REGIONSTATS is not available and some geography functions have local limits.

operations.label: change streams
limitations: Tables with change_stream_config (1 to 7 day retention) record one grouped record per row commit, garbage-collection and DropRowRange records, heartbeats with continuation tokens and low watermarks; ReadChangeStream resumes from tokens and closes at end_time, and needs a single-cluster app profile. One partition covers the whole key space, so split and merge are not exercised.

operations.label: snapshots and backups
limitations: Backups are immutable schema and row snapshots with create, get, list, update, copy, delete and restore to an independent table, including expire-time and backup-type rules. Tables with an automated backup policy get one backup per cluster every 24 hours while the emulator runs. UndeleteTable restores a deleted table within 7 days. Legacy table snapshot RPCs return Unimplemented. The REST backup listing ignores filter, order and pagination.

operations.label: IAM policy management
limitations: Policies on existing instances, tables, views and backups persist with etags (Aborted on mismatch) and update masks, and missing resources return NotFound. Policies are not evaluated: TestIamPermissions grants every requested permission. In strict IAM mode the gateway's port 5385 requires an identified caller and applies the strict-mode policy file.

operations.label: new proto methods return Unimplemented (no panics)
limitations: Every registered RPC of the Bigtable API has a defined outcome. Intentionally unsupported RPCs (legacy snapshots, hot tablets, memory layers) return Unimplemented instead of failing. ListLocations and PingAndWarm are served.

services.name: Spanner

persistence.backingStore: LevelDB rows plus JSON metadata at /var/lib/localcloud/spanner-data
persistence.restartBehavior: Instances, databases, schema, rows, backups, IAM policies, change-stream history and queue messages survive process and container restarts while the LocalCloud volume is retained.
recoveryLimitations: Row writes are not synced against host power loss.
Project checkpoints and exports do not capture Spanner data; Spanner backups are the in-product copy.

limitations: A PROTO or ENUM column cannot hold a value: a commit that writes a non-NULL PROTO or ENUM value fails with UNIMPLEMENTED and nothing of that commit is stored. Tables with such columns can be created, and rows that leave them NULL are stored.

Database roles and fine-grained access control are enforced for sessions created with a creator_role. Stored instance and database IAM policies are returned but not evaluated, and TestIamPermissions returns the requested permissions. In strict IAM mode the gateway's ports 5386 (gRPC) and 5387 (REST) require an identified caller and apply the strict-mode policy file.
Change streams require ExecuteStreamingSql; unary ExecuteSql rejects change-stream queries. Partition churn is timer-driven, not load-driven.
Backups are full database copies. Customer-managed encryption keys are not implemented, so data is stored in plaintext.

PartitionRead and PartitionQuery return one empty and one full partition. Directed reads, Data Boost, MoveInstance, AddSplitPoints, locality groups and optimizer hints are accepted without the physical effect.
ML.PREDICT, AI functions and remote functions return deterministic placeholder results unless remote_functions_host_port names a local adapter in the Spanner service config.
Cloud-only infrastructure (TrueTime, multi-region quorums, physical split points, tablet distribution, cross-region migration, autoscaling and quotas) does not apply to local development.
Project exports and checkpoints do not capture Spanner; they name it under not_captured_services. Use Spanner backups to keep data.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: Native SQL, read, and streaming read
limitations: Read, StreamingRead, ExecuteSql and ExecuteStreamingSql in the GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects, with resume tokens at row boundaries. Unary ExecuteSql rejects change-stream queries. Full-text search (TOKENIZE_*, SEARCH, SNIPPET, SCORE), vector search (APPROX_*), property graphs and the documented graph algorithms compute locally, as do TTL row deletion, query plans and SPANNER_SYS statistics. Search works over rows written before a restart.

operations.label: Sessions, transactions, and batch DML
limitations: Sessions (including batch create and multiplexed), read-write, read-only and single-use transactions. SERIALIZABLE (default) and REPEATABLE_READ isolation with wound-wait lock waits. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and LOCK_SCANNED_RANGES=exclusive take exclusive locks. Commit-timestamp columns (allow_commit_timestamp) and commit stats are supported; a deadlock aborts exactly one transaction, and unique indexes are checked at commit.

operations.label: Partition query/read and batch write
limitations: PartitionRead and PartitionQuery return valid tokens, one empty and one full partition, with no real parallel partitioning. Partitioned DML (including parameterized PostgreSQL statements) and BatchWrite are supported.

operations.label: Instance, configuration, and instance-partition administration
limitations: Instance and instance-partition administration, custom instance configurations and AIP-160 filters on list calls. gcloud reaches the admin API through the REST port 5387. MoveInstance updates configuration metadata without moving data, and capacity settings have no physical effect.

operations.label: Database administration and DDL
limitations: Database creation, DDL in GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL, drop protection (a protected database delete answers FAILED_PRECONDITION, also through instance deletion), ListDatabaseOperations, split points stored in SPANNER_SYS.USER_SPLIT_POINTS without physical pre-splitting, and database roles (CREATE and DROP ROLE, GRANT and REVOKE, ListDatabaseRoles).

operations.label: Instance and database IAM policies
limitations: Instance and database IAM policies are stored durably and returned through native endpoints with etag checks, but not evaluated; TestIamPermissions returns the requested permissions. Fine-grained access control is enforced for sessions created with a creator_role on queries, DML, reads, mutations and change-stream reads. In strict IAM mode the gateway requires an identified caller on 5386 and 5387.

operations.label: Backup, copy, restore, and backup schedules
limitations: CreateBackup (including version_time), CopyBackup, GetBackup, ListBackups with AIP-160 filters, UpdateBackup, DeleteBackup, RestoreDatabase and ListBackupOperations, plus full and incremental backup schedules that persist across restarts. Every backup is physically a full copy, and CMEK is not implemented.

operations.label: Long-running operation lifecycle
limitations: Long-running operations for instance, database, backup, copy and restore calls, with AIP-160 filters. CancelOperation has no effect because operations finish before it can act.

services.name: Google Sheets

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (cells of each sheet)
persistence.restartBehavior: Spreadsheet values survive a restart while the volume is kept.
recoveryLimitations: Data in the pre-0.1.10 Sheets format is refused rather than converted; delete it or reset Sheets before starting 0.1.10.

limitations: Google Sheets is provided as an auxiliary integration API for data lookups and BigQuery external-table fixtures, not as a Google Cloud service LocalCloud reproduces in full.

Served: spreadsheets.values.get, values.batchGet and values.update (PUT) under /v4/spreadsheets/{id}/values. Spreadsheet metadata (spreadsheets.get, create, batchUpdate), values.append, values.clear, values.batchUpdate and formula evaluation are not served.

Values are stored and returned as written (strings, numbers, booleans). valueInputOption and valueRenderOption are ignored, so a formula is kept as text and numbers are not returned as formatted strings.

Ranges accept sheet names, cells, cell ranges, whole columns or rows and whole sheets; a range with no sheet name addresses Sheet1. Reads honour majorDimension and return rows trimmed to their last populated cell. An empty range of a known spreadsheet answers 200 without values, and a spreadsheet the project does not hold answers 404. A read past the per-request limits (for example 100,000 rows) answers 400.

A spreadsheet exists once a write or seed stores one of its sheets. Its project comes from the X-Goog-User-Project header or the project query parameter, else the gateway's default project. Calls are not authorized per spreadsheet; Google OAuth scopes and Drive sharing are not modeled.

Release 0.1.10 stores values per cell and does not convert the earlier Sheets format: a database that still holds old Sheets rows stops at the startup migration with a message naming the DELETE statement to run.
A seed replaces each declared range's cells (an empty values list clears the range) and is checked before any range is written. Sheets data is not included in GET /export or project checkpoints.
