operations.label: spreadsheets.values.get
limitations: Reads any A1 range of the stored cells, including sub-ranges of earlier writes, whole columns, rows and sheets, with majorDimension ROWS or COLUMNS. Values come back as written; render options are ignored.

operations.label: spreadsheets.values.batchGet
limitations: Reads each ranges query parameter of one spreadsheet in order, under one shared read budget; any range that cannot be read fails the whole request. Values come back as written; render options are ignored.

operations.label: spreadsheets.values.update
limitations: PUT /v4/spreadsheets/{id}/values/{range} writes values from the range's top-left cell, ROWS or COLUMNS; an empty string clears a cell, null leaves it unchanged, and cells outside the written values keep theirs. The answer reports updatedRange, updatedRows, updatedColumns and updatedCells. valueInputOption is ignored, so formulas are stored as text.

services.name: Secret Manager

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (secrets, versions and payloads; CMEK versions store ciphertext and a wrapped data key)
persistence.restartBehavior: Secrets, versions and payload values survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept.
recoveryLimitations: A CMEK-protected version is readable only while its local Cloud KMS key version exists and is enabled; losing or clearing KMS state makes those payloads unreadable.
Project checkpoints do not capture Secret Manager; a checkpoint names the service as not captured.

limitations: Per-secret IAM policies are stored and returned, and strict mode decides the policy methods themselves, but secret and version reads and writes are not checked against those per-secret bindings; in strict mode they follow the gateway's policy file like other data-plane calls.
Rotation is metadata only: rotation.rotationPeriod is stored and returned, while nextRotationTime and topics are accepted and not kept, and no SECRET_ROTATE or version events are published.
Version aliases, annotations, tags and versionDestroyTtl sent through the API are not kept, so delayed version destruction is not available.

Regional endpoints (projects/{project}/locations/{location}/secrets) are accepted but address the same project-level secrets, and returned names have no location. Replication settings are stored; storage is local, so geographic replication and Google key custody are not provided.
Payloads are stored unencrypted in the data volume unless the secret uses a customer-managed key from local Cloud KMS.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: secrets.create/list/get/delete
limitations: Create, get, list, update and delete over gRPC and REST through one field mapping: labels, replication (automatic or user-managed, one customer-managed key per secret), expireTime or ttl, and rotation are stored. Updates apply only the fields their update mask names. List filters accept labels.KEY and name terms with =, : and !=; any other expression is 400. Secrets carry an etag and a delete with a stale etag is refused (409 over REST, ABORTED over gRPC). An expired secret is NOT_FOUND on every method and its ID can be reused. Secret IDs containing a slash are refused.

operations.label: versions.add/access/list
limitations: addVersion, get, list (pageSize, pageToken and nextPageToken), access (including latest), enable, disable and destroy over gRPC and REST. Payloads are capped at 64 KiB (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT beyond) and a supplied dataCrc32c must match; access returns the payload's CRC32C. Disabled and destroyed versions refuse access with FAILED_PRECONDITION and only a missing version is NOT_FOUND.

operations.label: rotation, CMEK, per-secret IAM
limitations: Customer-managed encryption uses a SOFTWARE key from local Cloud KMS; in strict mode the Secret Manager service agent needs the key's encrypter/decrypter grant. Per-secret setIamPolicy, getIamPolicy and testIamPermissions use the shared IAM policy store; a policy can be set only on an existing secret and is removed when the secret is deleted. Secret data calls are not checked against per-secret bindings. Rotation periods are stored, but no rotation notifications are delivered.

services.name: Cloud Tasks

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (queues, tasks, reserved task IDs and attempt activity)
persistence.restartBehavior: Queues, task bodies and task state are reloaded after a restart while the volume is kept. A task that was being delivered when LocalCloud stopped is offered again, so it can be delivered twice.
recoveryLimitations: Persistence does not undo external HTTP side effects or provide production delivery, retry, ordering or disaster-recovery guarantees.

limitations: Task and queue OAuth/OIDC credentials are minted by the LocalCloud issuer, not Google, and verify only against LocalCloud's JWKS. A queue httpTarget credential overrides task credentials and every task Authorization header; at queue level both the service account and the audience (OIDC) or scope (OAuth) are required. The OIDC audience defaults to the URL the request is sent to, after queue overrides, and the OAuth scope to cloud-platform. When no token can be minted (account missing or disabled, identity not ready) the request is not sent and the attempt records IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason> with normal retry. In strict mode, configuring a credential on a task or queue needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the account.
Redirect responses are followed (up to 10 hops) and the final answer decides the attempt.
App Engine tasks, appEngineRoutingOverride, stackdriverLoggingConfig (logging sampling) and cmekConfig are refused with UNIMPLEMENTED rather than stored.

/v2beta3 is served over REST only. Pull queues (Task.pullMessage), readMask and Queue.stats, the queues.list filter, tasks.batchCreate and tasks.batchDelete answer 501 there, and v2beta3 queues report type PUSH. Locations and operations are served on neither version.

BufferTask is served on /v2 and /v2beta3 (POST tasks:buffer and tasks/{id}:buffer) and answers FAILED_PRECONDITION when the queue's httpTarget has no uriOverride host. The X-CloudTasks-TaskRetryReason header is not sent.

Queue IDs allow letters, digits and hyphens (up to 100 characters); an ID with an underscore is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT. Task IDs may contain underscores. A task ID stays reserved for one hour after its task is deleted, completes or exhausts its retries, and a create with it answers ALREADY_EXISTS; a purge reserves no IDs. The task_name_reuse_window_seconds setting is accepted but has no effect.

No FIFO, exactly-once, dead-letter queue, transactional cancellation, adaptive Google throttling or production throughput guarantees. A schedule time must be within 30 days. Unlimited retry settings have no automatic task expiry.

HTTP dispatch deadlines are 15 to 1800 seconds (default 600). Failed attempts use the configured fractional backoff; when both an attempt limit and a duration limit are set, both must be exhausted. A zero duration leaves only the attempt limit, and maxAttempts -1 is unlimited.

Completed attempt metadata stays in the local activity view until cleared by default; the cloudtasks setting activity_retention_days (default 0) limits it. The view holds no request URL, headers, payload or response body. Successful and exhausted tasks leave the queue, so absence alone is not success.

Queued tasks and tasks interrupted during delivery are reloaded after a restart and delivered again, so handlers must tolerate duplicates. Pause, purge and delete do not cancel requests already in flight.

BASIC views omit the payload, headers and OAuth/OIDC configuration; FULL needs cloudtasks.tasks.fullView in strict mode. In strict mode every queue and task call, REST or gRPC, is decided for the verified caller against stored IAM policies, and anonymous calls are refused (PERMISSION_DENIED, HTTP 403). Open and permissive modes do not check.

A seed creates queues by name and location with default settings and leaves an existing queue unchanged; it does not set httpTarget, rate or retry settings. Queues and tasks are not included in GET /export or project checkpoints, which report Cloud Tasks as not captured.
Request bodies over 4 MiB answer 413. A storage failure answers UNAVAILABLE (HTTP 503) so clients retry.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: queues.create/get/list/update/pause/resume/purge/delete
limitations: REST (/v2 and /v2beta3) and gRPC (v2) share project- and location-scoped queue lifecycle, rate limits, retry config and the queue IAM verbs (getIamPolicy, setIamPolicy, testIamPermissions). Queue httpTarget uriOverride (scheme, host, port, path, query, ALWAYS and IF_NOT_EXISTS), httpMethod, headerOverrides and oauthToken or oidcToken are stored, returned, survive a restart and apply at delivery, with update masks such as http_target, http_target.oauth_token and http_target.oidc_token. Queue state is output-only. App Engine routing, logging sampling and cmekConfig are refused.

operations.label: tasks.create/get/list/delete/run
limitations: Durable HTTP task creation, BASIC/FULL views, pagination and immediate run. Automatic dispatch honours queue rate, concurrency and fractional retry settings, and the activity view records each observed HTTP outcome. Task httpRequest.oidcToken and oauthToken deliver local-issuer tokens minted per attempt. BufferTask turns a raw request body into a task on a queue whose httpTarget has a host. Deliveries carry X-CloudTasks-QueueName, TaskName, TaskRetryCount, TaskExecutionCount, TaskETA and, after a response, TaskPreviousResponse, with User-Agent Google-Cloud-Tasks. App Engine tasks are refused with UNIMPLEMENTED.

services.name: Cloud Scheduler

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (jobs, queued runs and execution history)
persistence.restartBehavior: Jobs, queued runs, retries and history are reloaded after a restart while the volume is kept. A run interrupted during delivery is recorded as UNKNOWN and not replayed; a job that came due while LocalCloud was stopped runs once.
recoveryLimitations: External side effects of deliveries have their own lifecycle; persistence does not undo or confirm them.

limitations: Schedules use five-field UNIX cron and IANA time zones from the image's time-zone data; preview and dispatch share one parser. The forms every N minutes (1 to 59), every N hours (1 to 23), every day HH:MM and every DAY[,DAY...] HH:MM are converted to cron in the job's time zone; other English-like schedules are refused with a message listing these forms.
HTTP and Pub/Sub targets deliver for real. App Engine targets are refused before saving.

httpTarget oidcToken and oauthToken are stored with the job and minted at each attempt by the LocalCloud issuer, not Google, so receivers must trust the local issuer and JWKS. The OIDC audience defaults to the target URI and the OAuth scope to cloud-platform; the generated header is the only Authorization header, and a user Authorization header is refused. Create and update refuse a token for an account that does not exist or is disabled (PERMISSION_DENIED) in every IAM mode; no iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission is evaluated. At delivery a missing or disabled account, or unavailable identity, fails the attempt with IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason> through normal retry and history, and nothing is sent.

Queued runs and retries survive a restart. An attempt interrupted while running is recorded as UNKNOWN and not replayed, because the target may already have received it. A scheduled time that arrives while an earlier scheduled run of the job is still running or retrying waits as one queued run, and later times fold into it; manual runs can overlap. A job whose time passed while LocalCloud was stopped runs once after the start; the other missed times are not backfilled.

Retry count is 0 to 5, max doublings 0 to 16 and backoff 0 to 86400 seconds; fractional and explicit zero durations are kept. Retry duration starts with the first actual attempt, and when both count and duration are set both limits must be exhausted. HTTP attempt deadlines are 15 to 1800 seconds (default 180); Pub/Sub targets ignore attemptDeadline. Up to 16 deliveries run in parallel.

Full project/location/job names scope jobs and history; location names are namespaces, not residency guarantees. There is no per-job IAM: in strict mode the gateway checks the caller's verified LocalCloud credential against its access-policy rules.

HTTP deliveries carry X-CloudScheduler-JobName and X-CloudScheduler-RunId headers. The local history view returns at most the newest 100 attempts of a job. Every execution is kept by default; the cloudscheduler setting executions_keep_per_job (default 0) limits it.
A seed creates the jobs it declares and reports an invalid job by name. Jobs are not included in GET /export or project checkpoints.
Request bodies over 4 MiB, including jobs:preview, answer 413.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: jobs.create/list/get/update/delete/pause/resume/run
limitations: REST and gRPC validate a job before saving it and schedule real HTTP and Pub/Sub delivery. Full readback, masked updates (REST camelCase paths are accepted), a cron preview route, per-job history, durable queued retries and HTTP deadlines. Updates, pause, resume, delete and the scheduler tick are serialized per job, so a pause or delete is never undone by a due run. HTTP targets accept oidcToken or oauthToken, and each manual, scheduled or retried attempt sends one Authorization header signed by the local issuer; a target that refuses it (HTTP 401 or 403) is recorded as a failed attempt. App Engine targets are refused.

services.name: Cloud Functions (2nd Gen)

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (function catalog and Firestore trigger delivery state)
persistence.restartBehavior: Functions and trigger registrations reload after a restart while the volume is kept; managed Pub/Sub trigger subscriptions are reconciled at start, and undelivered Firestore trigger events resume with the same event IDs. Function processes run outside LocalCloud and are not restarted by it.
recoveryLimitations: External function processes and their side effects have their own lifecycle and recovery.

limitations: LocalCloud stores function metadata and forwards invocations to a target you run; it never builds source or starts, stops or supervises a function process. serviceConfig.uri names the target (default: the LOCALCLOUD_FUNCTION_<ID>_ENDPOINT environment value of the gateway, else http://localhost:8081), and serviceConfig.service naming a LocalCloud Cloud Run service forwards to that service. GenerateUploadUrl and GenerateDownloadUrl return placeholder URLs; nothing is uploaded or built.

Triggers: HTTP; Pub/Sub google.cloud.pubsub.topic.v1.messagePublished on a topic of the function's project; and Firestore google.cloud.firestore.document.v1.created, updated, deleted and written with database, namespace ((default) only) and document filters, including match-path-pattern. Firestore events come from the LocalCloud Firestore service, which is opt-in. Storage, Audit Log and other Eventarc event types are refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT (400) and create no function or subscription.

Firestore events are sent as binary-mode CloudEvents (ce-* headers) with JSON data holding value, oldValue and updateMask, not the application/protobuf payload Google sends, so a handler that decodes protobuf event data needs a JSON path locally. They reach only a loopback target or a registered Cloud Run service. With retryPolicy RETRY_POLICY_RETRY a failed delivery retries with backoff from 10 to 600 seconds for 24 hours; otherwise, and after that window, it stays listed at GET /functions/firestore/deliveries for a manual POST /functions/firestore/deliveries/retry. Handlers must tolerate duplicate event IDs.

Functions are invoked with POST on their url, http://localhost:{gateway port}/functions/trigger/{project}/{location}/{function}, and the call is forwarded to the target as a POST with the body. The caller's Authorization header reaches the target unchanged and X-Serverless-Authorization without its signature; cookies and LocalCloud caller headers are not forwarded. Open and permissive modes forward every call. Strict mode requires a LocalCloud ID token (X-Serverless-Authorization, else Authorization) whose audience is the function URL, serviceConfig.uri or the Cloud Run service URL (401 otherwise) and cloudfunctions.functions.invoke on the function (403; roles/cloudfunctions.invoker grants it). gcp-live answers 503.

A Pub/Sub trigger creates a managed push subscription that pushes an ID token for eventTrigger.serviceAccountEmail with the function URL as audience. With no serviceAccountEmail it pushes without a token, which strict mode refuses, and no iam.serviceAccounts.actAs check is made for the trigger account. Deleting and recreating the topic re-attaches the trigger.

serviceConfig.uri must be an http or https URL without credentials. A target on the gateway's port or the LocalCloud listener range 5380 to 5410, or on an unspecified, multicast or link-local address (metadata servers included), is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT at create and update and again at connection time, redirects included. Relayed responses are capped at 32 MiB.

serviceConfig.serviceAccountEmail gives the external process no credentials by itself. Register an identity session with POST /identity/sessions and a function field to serve Application Default Credentials for the function's runtime account; readback reports this state in stateMessages (type LocalCloudExternalRuntime).

Create and delete span the function catalog and the managed Pub/Sub subscription and roll back on failure. A delete that fails part-way leaves the function DELETING and answers UNAVAILABLE; retrying completes it, and messages queued for the trigger are kept meanwhile.
Seeds create functions. Functions are not included in GET /export or project checkpoints.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: functions.create/list/get/delete/update
limitations: Second-generation function create, get, list, update and delete over REST and gRPC (long-running operations), with nested update masks such as serviceConfig.maxInstanceCount and labels.team; an unknown mask path is INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything changes. The function url is http://localhost:{gateway port}/functions/trigger/{project}/{location}/{function}, and calls there are forwarded to serviceConfig.uri or a LocalCloud Cloud Run service, following the IAM mode rules in the limitations. A trigger call answers 503 when the function has no endpoint or the catalog is unavailable. Pub/Sub messagePublished triggers create a managed push subscription. Source builds and managed function execution are not provided.

operations.label: Firestore document triggers (google.cloud.firestore.document.v1.created/updated/deleted/written)
limitations: Registrations match a database, the (default) namespace and an exact document path or a match-path-pattern with captures and wildcards. Each committed change is delivered to every matching function as a binary-mode CloudEvent with JSON data (value, oldValue, updateMask), carrying a LocalCloud ID token for the trigger account (eventTrigger.serviceAccountEmail, else the runtime account, else default@{project}) with the function URL as audience, to a loopback target or a registered Cloud Run service. Delivery state is durable; failures retry for 24 hours with RETRY_POLICY_RETRY and can be listed and retried through /functions/firestore/deliveries. Google's protobuf event encoding is not produced.

services.name: AlloyDB

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud/pgdata: one database per cluster, plus cluster, instance, database, user and backup records
persistence.restartBehavior: Clusters with their databases and data, instances, users and backup records survive a restart with the LocalCloud volume; operations do not.
recoveryLimitations: Backups and restores do not copy database contents.
Project checkpoints and exports do not capture AlloyDB.

limitations: Each cluster is a PostgreSQL database on the bundled PostgreSQL server on port 5391, the same server that Cloud SQL PostgreSQL instances use. Its database name and the users' login role names are scoped by project, location and cluster and are not reported by the API.

Instances are records: they report READY and ipAddress 127.0.0.1 and start no separate server. getConnectionInfo returns only the IP address and there is no client certificate service, so AlloyDB connectors and the Auth Proxy cannot connect; connect directly to the PostgreSQL port.

Cluster, instance and backup IDs must match ^[a-z]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ (400 otherwise). A body that is not JSON answers 400 and one over 8 MiB answers 413. Creating an existing cluster, instance, user, database or backup answers 409 ALREADY_EXISTS.
clusters.patch and instances.patch change displayName and labels only. supportedDatabaseFlags.list returns a fixed list (max_connections, shared_buffers), and database flags are not applied.

clusters.restore and clusters.restoreFromCloudSQL create a new, empty cluster with the requested ID: the backup or Cloud SQL source is not read and no instances or data are restored. Backups store records only. Cluster export and import and instance restart return a done operation without doing work; other cluster collection verbs answer 404.
Each user gets a scoped PostgreSQL login role carrying its password. databaseRoles are recorded but not granted, so a user has PostgreSQL's default privileges on the cluster database.
Every operation is returned done. Operations are kept in memory, the newest 1000 (alloydb.operation_retention_hours adds an age limit), and are gone after a restart.
Project exports and checkpoints do not include AlloyDB; a seed can create clusters.
Secondary clusters, switchover, failover, fault injection, upgrades, read pools, replication and AlloyDB engine features such as the columnar engine are not emulated.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: clusters/instances.create/list/get/delete
limitations: Cluster and instance create, get, list and delete over REST and gRPC. Each cluster creates a PostgreSQL database on the bundled server (port 5391) and a cluster delete drops it; instances are records that start no separate server.

operations.label: clusters.patch/instances.patch/supportedDatabaseFlags.list/clusters.restore
limitations: Patch changes displayName and labels only. supportedDatabaseFlags.list returns a fixed two-flag list. clusters.restore creates a new empty cluster without reading the backup, and backups are records only.

operations.label: users.create/get/list/patch/delete
limitations: Each user gets a scoped PostgreSQL login role with its password; a password change updates the role first, and delete drops the role before the record. databaseRoles are recorded but not granted.

services.name: Dataproc

persistence.backingStore: Cluster, job (with driver output) and cluster-default records in the bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud/pgdata; cluster filesystems live in their Docker containers
persistence.restartBehavior: Cluster and job records survive a restart with the LocalCloud volume. Cluster containers are separate Docker containers; at startup they are checked against the records and RUNNING clusters without a running container are marked ERROR or STOPPED.
recoveryLimitations: Files written inside a cluster container are lost when the container is removed by a cluster delete, a start of an ERROR cluster or a reset.
Project checkpoints and exports do not capture Dataproc.

limitations: Requires Docker access. Each cluster runs as one Docker container (image agentcloud/dataproc:2.3.34-debian12, or the image LOCALCLOUD_DATAPROC_IMAGE names), pulled on first use. Worker counts, machine types and softwareConfig.imageVersion are recorded but add no nodes and select no other image, and the dataproc settings registry and prefer_native are not read.

sparkJob, pysparkJob (including inline Python), sparkSqlJob, hadoopJob and hiveJob run inside the cluster container; other job types answer 400. A job submitted without placement.clusterName runs in an on-demand default container, LocalCloud's serverless mode, without workload identity. The Batches, Sessions, WorkflowTemplates and AutoscalingPolicies APIs, DiagnoseCluster and SubmitJobAsOperation are not implemented.

With local workload identity, a cluster runs as config.gceClusterConfig.serviceAccount (default@{project}.iam.gserviceaccount.com when unset) with serviceAccountScopes (cloud-platform when unset). A relay container serves that account's tokens to the cluster at GCE_METADATA_HOST=127.0.0.1:8081 and is removed with the cluster; a cluster whose relay cannot start fails its boot. The account is not checked for existence or actAs, and a cluster naming a missing account boots but its jobs cannot get tokens.

Job code reaches Cloud Storage and BigQuery through STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST and BIGQUERY_EMULATOR_HOST, which send no credentials, so under strict IAM those calls are not made as the cluster's account. Driver output is written to the regional staging bucket path as the verified submitter, so in strict mode it is stored only where the submitter's grants allow; it stays readable through GET .../jobs/{jobId}/output.

Project, region, cluster name and job ID follow Dataproc's naming rules, and domain-scoped project IDs such as example.com:proj are refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT, REST 400). Starting or stopping a cluster that is booting or already changing answers FAILED_PRECONDITION (REST 412). A stored cluster record this version cannot read answers 412 on create, get, start and stop until the record is deleted.

clusters.create returns a long-running operation that finishes when the container and relay are up; start, stop and patch (updateMask) return operations too, and starting an ERROR cluster boots it again. After a gateway restart, a cluster that was still booting is ERROR, and RUNNING clusters whose container is missing or exited become ERROR or STOPPED. A job that was running when the gateway restarted is not tracked to completion; resubmit it.

Runtime profiles (/runtime/profiles) list Dataproc runtime images for runtime-migration runs (POST /migration/runs). Only PUBLISHED profiles with a usable image digest run; the published 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 profiles carry placeholder digests, so runs against them fail the image check. A run executes the suite's workload on the baseline and each target profile and judges log assertions and wall time; it does not capture, reset or restore project state between cases.
Autoscaling, multi-node scaling, automated node repair and Dataproc service-level guarantees are not emulated.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: clusters.create/list/get/delete
limitations: Create, get, list, delete, patch, start and stop over gRPC and REST (/v1/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/clusters), each cluster one Docker container with an identity relay when local workload identity is on. Create, start, stop and patch return long-running operations (REST create answers 202 with an operation named operations/{id}); DeleteCluster returns a done operation with an Empty response. LocalCloud extensions: portMappings on create, cluster-defaults, and consoles and metrics reads.

operations.label: jobs submit/list/get
limitations: jobs:submit, get, list (clusterName, jobStateMatcher and a filter on status.state, placement.clusterName, reference.jobId and labels), cancel and delete. Spark, PySpark, Spark SQL, Hadoop and Hive jobs run in the cluster container; jobs without a cluster run in an on-demand default container without workload identity. A job waits while its cluster is being created and is refused (412) on a STOPPED or ERROR cluster. Driver output is readable through jobs/{jobId}/output and copied to the staging bucket as the submitter.

services.name: Cloud IAM

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (service accounts, keys, custom roles, allow policies, workload identity pools and providers)
persistence.restartBehavior: Service accounts, keys, custom roles, allow policies, pools and providers survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept. Workload identity OAuth clients, namespaces, managed identities and attestation rules are held in memory and are lost on restart.
recoveryLimitations: A change is written to the database before it applies; a refused write answers 503 (UNAVAILABLE over gRPC) and leaves the previous state.
Project checkpoints do not capture Cloud IAM state; a checkpoint names the service as not captured.

limitations: The IAM mode is the cloudiam.mode setting: open (the default) allows every call, permissive allows every call and logs the decision, strict enforces local policy, and gcp-live fails closed. A mode change applies when Cloud IAM restarts; an unknown mode stops the gateway at startup.

Strict mode is a development mode, not a security boundary. A LocalCloud-signed token decides the caller on its own; a request with no credential is named by the X-LocalCloud-User header, which any client can set. An unsigned bearer string or a forged token-shaped value names no caller and is refused (401 or 403), and it never falls back to the header. A request with no token and no header is anonymous and refused.

In strict mode the stored allow policies decide Cloud IAM's own resources (service accounts, keys, credentials, roles, workload identity), Cloud KMS with Autokey and EKM, Cloud Storage buckets and objects, Cloud Tasks, Workflows actAs, long-running operations, and the policy methods of Secret Manager and Resource Manager. Other services' data calls are decided by the cloudiam.policy_file document, which maps identities to path prefixes: with no file, or a file without bindings, every identified caller is admitted; a file that cannot be read or parsed refuses identified callers until it loads. The admin and Console plane is exempt.
gcp-live never contacts Google. It refuses bearer tokens on routed paths, and the IAM policy, token minting and session routes fail closed, so it cannot be used for real Google delegation.

Conditions support request.time, resource.name, resource.type and resource.service with logical and comparison operators, startsWith, endsWith, timestamp and the exists and all macros; other CEL functions are refused when the policy is set. Policies inherit from a resource to its project. Organization and folder ancestry, deny policies, policy history, Policy Troubleshooter and recommendations are not served.

A project created in strict mode has no binding for its creator, unlike Google Cloud. Grant a project role such as roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin or roles/owner before reading or changing its policy.

Tokens are signed by this runtime's own issuer (server.identity.issuer_url) and verified against its JWKS at /oauth2/v3/certs. Receivers must trust the local issuer; Google-issued tokens are not accepted, and verifiers that hard-code Google certificates reject local tokens.

Workload identity token exchange is not served: /v1/token is the local OAuth token endpoint and answers unsupported_grant_type for the RFC 8693 token-exchange grant. Pools and providers are stored resources only.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy/testIamPermissions
limitations: Allow policies are stored per resource with etags and version 3 conditions, through REST and gRPC, and are inherited from a resource to its project. A policy with an unknown field (for example a misspelled condition key) is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and an expired conditional binding no longer grants. In strict and gcp-live, setIamPolicy and getIamPolicy need the resource's IAM permission for the verified caller. testIamPermissions in open and permissive returns the requested permissions unchanged; in strict it returns those the caller holds through the stored policies. iamPolicies:lintPolicy and iamPolicies:queryAuditableServices are served. Organization and folder policies, deny policies and policy history are not.

operations.label: roles.create/patch/delete/queryGrantableRoles
limitations: Project custom roles support create, get, list, patch, delete and undelete over REST and gRPC, persist across restarts and are cleared by a project reset; predefined roles are read-only (400 on change), and POST /v1/roles without a project is 404. queryGrantableRoles returns every predefined role plus the project's custom roles, not only the roles grantable on the named resource.

operations.label: serviceAccounts.patch/keys.enable/keys.disable/queryTestablePermissions
limitations: Service accounts support create, get, list, patch, delete, undelete, enable and disable over REST and gRPC; account IDs follow Google's rule (6 to 30 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter). Keys support create (a key file whose token_uri names the gateway port), upload, get, list (with the keyTypes filter), delete, enable and disable; undeleting an account restores only the keys its deletion removed. Lookups stay inside the named project, so a cross-project request is 404. In strict mode each method needs the iam.serviceAccounts.* or iam.serviceAccountKeys.* permission Google names for it, on the account or its project; a caller without it gets 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, also for a missing account. queryTestablePermissions lists every permission the local catalogue knows, not only those that apply to the named resource.

operations.label: iamcredentials projects.serviceAccounts.generateAccessToken/generateIdToken/signBlob/signJwt (REST and gRPC)
limitations: Mints locally signed access and ID tokens and signs blobs and JWTs for a service account over REST (projects/-/serviceAccounts/{account}) and gRPC; IAM v1 signBlob (bytesToSign) and signJwt on a named project are served on the same paths. Token lifetimes come from server.identity.access_token_lifetime_seconds and id_token_lifetime_seconds (3600 s by default); requested lifetime, scope, delegates and includeEmail are not applied. generateIdToken needs an audience (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise), a disabled account is 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION and a missing one is 404. Signing uses one SYSTEM_MANAGED key per account, created on first use and published at /service_accounts/v1/metadata/x509/{email} and /service_accounts/v1/metadata/jwk/{email}. In strict mode each method needs iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken, getOpenIdToken, signBlob or signJwt on the account; gcp-live refuses minting. The OAuth JWT-bearer grant at /oauth2/token accepts assertions signed with a registered account key.

operations.label: sts v1 token (RFC 8693) and iam projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools/providers create/get/list/patch/delete/undelete
limitations: Workload identity pools and providers support create, get, list (with showDeleted), patch, delete and undelete, persist across restarts, and return completed operations. Pool and provider IDs follow Google's rule (4 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, no gcp- prefix; 400 otherwise), a repeated create is 409 ALREADY_EXISTS, an unknown name is 404, and a provider needs its pool. Provider settings are stored as given and are not evaluated. The STS token exchange is not served: /v1/token answers unsupported_grant_type for the token-exchange grant, so external subject tokens cannot be exchanged locally. OAuth clients, namespaces and managed identities are served from memory only.

services.name: Cloud Resource Manager

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (project records)
persistence.restartBehavior: Project records survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept. crm- operations are held in memory and are lost on restart.
recoveryLimitations: A reset removes every project record and restores the built-in default projects.
A store failure is reported and the change is not kept in memory.

limitations: Projects only: organizations, folders, moves, liens, tag bindings and full ancestry are not modelled. Every project reports an organization parent with ID 0, and list and search return every project without filtering.

Creating a project whose ID exists returns the existing project in a completed operation instead of ALREADY_EXISTS. Project IDs are not checked against Google's project ID rule by this API; the admin routes refuse IDs outside the local pattern.

Deleting a project is immediate: it resets every service's data for that project and removes the record, with no DELETE_REQUESTED state and no undelete. The configured default project cannot be deleted (403), and an unknown project is 404.

Requests the gateway serves register an unrecorded, well-formed project ID on first use when server.auto_provision_projects is true (the default), in every IAM mode once the request is authorized; only a project marker at the start of the path or after an API version counts.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: projects.create/list/get/update/delete
limitations: Projects support create, get, list, search, update and delete over v1 and v3 REST and gRPC; v1 accepts name and v3 accepts displayName for the display name. Create and delete return completed operations (crm- prefixed, pollable over REST), as does a gRPC update; a REST update returns the project. A gRPC update writes only the fields its update mask names, and labels.KEY changes only that key. Project getIamPolicy, setIamPolicy and testIamPermissions use the shared IAM policy store over REST and gRPC, with the strict and gcp-live checks. An existing ID returns the existing project; delete is immediate and clears the project's data.

services.name: Service Usage

persistence.backingStore: Gateway service configuration in the LocalCloud data volume (one enabled switch per service); operations are held in memory
persistence.restartBehavior: A service disabled or enabled through Service Usage keeps that state after a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept. Enable and disable operations are lost on restart.
recoveryLimitations: The switch is shared with the Console and admin service controls, so either path changes what Service Usage reports.

limitations: Each served API maps to one gateway service switch shared by every project: disabling pubsub.googleapis.com in one project turns Pub/Sub off for all projects until it is enabled again, and the change persists across restarts.

Disabling iam.googleapis.com, cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com, serviceusage.googleapis.com or another always-on API completes as a no-op and the API stays ENABLED. A Google-shaped API name the gateway does not serve reports ENABLED and enable or disable succeeds without effect, so a misspelled name of that shape also reports ENABLED; a name that is not shaped like a Google API is NOT_FOUND.
services.list returns every API name the gateway serves or always reports, with its state; filter and paging parameters are not applied.
Consumer quota metrics return an empty list; quotas, quota overrides, billing and project entitlements are not modelled.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: services.enable/disable/list
limitations: services.get, list, batchGet, enable, disable and batchEnable report and change the gateway's own service state; a disabled service refuses its API calls until it is enabled again. Cloud SQL resolves as sqladmin (sql is accepted too). Enable, disable and batchEnable return completed operations, readable at /v1/operations/su-*; a batch that fails part way names the services it enabled. The switch is gateway-wide, not per project.

services.name: Cloud Billing

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (budgets and project billing links)
persistence.restartBehavior: Budgets and project billing links survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept.
recoveryLimitations: A project reset removes that project's billing link; a never-linked project reports the local billing account.

limitations: Billing is metadata only: there are no prices, charges or cost accumulation, budget thresholds never fire, no notifications or Pub/Sub messages are sent, and billing export is not simulated.
There is one local billing account. billingAccounts.list and get return it, any other account is 404, and billingAccounts.projects.list returns an empty list.

Budgets keep displayName, amount, thresholdRules and an owning project taken from the first budgetFilter project; other budget fields such as notificationsRule and the rest of budgetFilter are not stored.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: billing accounts and budgets CRUD
limitations: Budgets support create, get, list, patch and delete under billingAccounts/{account}/budgets with displayName, amount and thresholdRules. The local billing account is listed and readable. Spend, threshold evaluation and notifications are not modelled.

operations.label: projects.getBillingInfo/updateBillingInfo
limitations: PUT /v1/projects/{project}/billingInfo stores the project's billing account and GET reads it back. An empty billingAccountName unlinks the project and reports billingEnabled false; a name that is not billingAccounts/{id} or a body that is not JSON is 400. The named account need not exist locally.

services.name: Cloud Logging

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (log entries, sinks and logs-based metrics), with entries also held in memory
persistence.restartBehavior: Entries, sinks and metrics survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept; startup loads the entries inside the retention window, newest first, up to the application budget.
recoveryLimitations: Entries removed by a retention period or size budget are deleted from PostgreSQL and cannot be recovered.

limitations: Served over gRPC: WriteLogEntries, ListLogEntries, ListLogs, DeleteLog, sinks (create, get, list, update, delete) and logs-based metrics (create, get, list, update, delete). Served over REST: entries:write, entries:list and projects/{project}/sinks create, get, list and delete. REST sink updates, REST logs-based metrics and REST logs routes are not served (404), so clients that manage sinks or metrics over REST, such as gcloud and Terraform, need the gRPC client libraries instead.
Exclusions, log buckets and views, TailLogEntries and the other ConfigServiceV2 RPCs answer UNIMPLEMENTED.

entries:list and ListLogEntries need resourceNames naming at least one project (INVALID_ARGUMENT / 400 otherwise). The filter supports AND, OR, NOT, a leading minus and parentheses over logName, severity, resource.type, resource.labels.KEY, labels.KEY, textPayload, insertId, trace, spanId, timestamp, jsonPayload.PATH and protoPayload.PATH, plus free-text terms. Ordering comparisons on strings, httpRequest and operation fields, regular expressions and functions are refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT (400); a filter is never applied in part. Filters are limited to 16 KiB and 100 nesting levels.

Sinks store every LogSink field and reads return them, but no entry is delivered to any destination; disabled and exclusions change nothing. Sink IDs are 1 to 100 letters, digits, underscores, hyphens or periods. A logs-based metric is a stored definition: no metric values or Cloud Monitoring time series are derived from log entries.

Retention defaults to forever (application_retention_days and runtime_retention_days 0). Size budgets default to 512 MiB for application logs and 128 MiB for LocalCloud runtime logs; past a budget the oldest entries are removed from memory and from PostgreSQL, and 0 sets no budget. Set application_retention_days to 30 to match the _Default bucket.
REST bodies are limited to 1 MiB (10 MiB for entries:write) and answer 413 beyond that. LocalCloud runtime diagnostics are kept under their own scope and do not appear in project listings.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: write log entries and list/filter entries
limitations: Entries keep their text, JSON or proto payload (a protoPayload of an unknown type is kept as its type URL and bytes), resource, labels, operation, httpRequest, sourceLocation, split, trace, spanId, traceSampled and nanosecond timestamp, and read back over gRPC and REST. An entry needs a log name. Listings apply the parsed filter, orderBy timestamp asc or desc, pageSize (100 by default) and page tokens; an unknown page token is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

operations.label: logs-based metric create/get/list/update/delete (MetricsServiceV2 gRPC and REST)
limitations: Served over gRPC only; the REST metrics routes are not served. Definitions are stored per project with every field and returned as written; an update replaces the definition and needs a filter. No metric values are derived from log entries.

operations.label: sink create/get/list/update/delete (ConfigServiceV2 gRPC; REST create/get/list/delete)
limitations: Sinks are stored with every LogSink field plus createTime and updateTime and read back as written. A duplicate ID is ALREADY_EXISTS. gRPC UpdateSink applies the update mask (an empty mask sets destination, filter and includeChildren; an unknown path is INVALID_ARGUMENT). No entries are exported to the destination.

services.name: Cloud Monitoring

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (time series, points, metric descriptors, alert policies, notification channels)
persistence.restartBehavior: Time series, points, descriptors, alert policies and channels survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept.
recoveryLimitations: Points are kept without a retention limit; a project reset removes them.

limitations: Served over gRPC and REST v3: time series create and list, metric descriptors create, get, list and delete, alert policies and notification channels create, get, list, update and delete. Groups, uptime checks, services and SLOs, snoozes and channel verification are not served.

ListTimeSeries filters support =, != and : on metric.type, resource.type, metric.labels.KEY and resource.labels.KEY, joined by AND, OR and NOT with parentheses. Other fields and functions such as starts_with and one_of are refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT (400). An aligner or reducer other than NONE, groupByFields or orderBy is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED (501); points are returned raw.

Alert policies are not evaluated and notification channels send nothing. Alert policy and channel list filters and orderBy are ignored. REST PATCH on an alert policy merges the body fields and ignores updateMask; gRPC updates apply the mask.
A metric descriptor get returns the created descriptor, else one derived from the type's written series, else NOT_FOUND, including for built-in metric types with no series.
The Console and /browse/monitoring return the newest 200 points of each of the first 200 matching series by default (limit and seriesLimit, up to 1000 each).
Dashboards, uptime execution and Google's distributed probes run only in Google Cloud.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: create/list time series and descriptors
limitations: Every TypedValue case (bool, int64, double, string, distribution), metricKind, valueType and unit are stored and returned as written, with nanosecond point times; a nanos value outside 0 to 999999999 refuses the whole write. A series is identified by project, metric type and labels, resource type and labels. ListTimeSeries applies the filter, interval, FULL and HEADERS views and page tokens. Descriptors can be created, read, listed and deleted, and a descriptor is derived for each written metric type that has none.

operations.label: alert policy create/get/list/update/delete (AlertPolicyService gRPC and REST)
limitations: Display name (required), conditions, combiner, notification channels, documentation, enabled, user labels, severity and alert strategy are stored and shared by gRPC and REST. Every named notification channel must exist in the project (INVALID_ARGUMENT / 400). Policies are not evaluated.

operations.label: notification channel create/get/list/update/delete (NotificationChannelService gRPC and REST)
limitations: Channels of any type are stored and read back with their labels and enabled flag. Deleting a channel that a policy names is FAILED_PRECONDITION unless force is set, which also removes it from those policies. No notification is ever sent and verification RPCs are not served.

services.name: GKE

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (cluster records); k3d cluster containers run on the host Docker daemon
persistence.restartBehavior: Cluster records survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept; k3d clusters keep running on Docker. GKE operations are memory-only and are lost on restart.
recoveryLimitations: k3d clusters are Docker containers with their own lifecycle: removing them outside LocalCloud leaves a record whose endpoint no longer answers.
A delete removes the record only after the k3d teardown succeeds, so a failed or interrupted delete can be retried.

limitations: GKE is opt-in. Real clusters need Docker access and the k3d CLI, which the full LocalCloud image includes. Provisioning runs after CreateCluster answers; a k3d failure ends the operation DONE with the k3d output in its statusMessage and leaves the cluster in ERROR until it is deleted.

Without k3d (the lite image) a create still succeeds: the cluster becomes RUNNING with a status message saying it is a simulated cluster with metadata only and no Kubernetes API. Seeded sample clusters are also metadata-only records.
Every cluster is one k3d server node running the pinned k3s image rancher/k3s:v1.32.5-k3s1. initialNodeCount is stored and reported as initialNodeCount and currentNodeCount but is not applied.

The reported Kubernetes version is not the running one: reads return the requested initialClusterVersion (1.28 when none is given) as the master and node version, and GetServerConfig lists 1.28, 1.27 and 1.26, while every cluster serves Kubernetes v1.32.5.

Each cluster's Kubernetes API listens on a loopback port of the Docker host from 5443 to 5465 (the k3d port range); Cluster.endpoint names it. Clients reach it with the kubeconfig k3d writes for the cluster, whose k3d name /browse/gke reports; GKE credentials minted by gcloud are not accepted by k3s.

GKE and AlloyDB share the REST path /v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/clusters, which the gateway gives to AlloyDB. Regional GKE REST is served under /container/v1 (GOOGLE_CONTAINER_CUSTOM_ENDPOINT, or CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_CONTAINER=<gateway>/container/); zonal /projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/clusters routes are served under both /v1 and /container/v1. GKE gRPC is unaffected.

Implemented: CreateCluster, GetCluster, ListClusters, DeleteCluster, GetOperation, ListOperations, CancelOperation and GetServerConfig. UpdateCluster, every node-pool RPC and the other ClusterManager RPCs answer UNIMPLEMENTED over gRPC, and their REST paths are not served (404). GetJSONWebKeys returns a placeholder key.

Pod workload identity is not implemented: workloadIdentityConfig.workloadPool is validated ({project}.svc.id.goog) and stored, but no admission webhook, metadata relay or token exchange runs inside clusters, so pods get no Application Default Credentials from LocalCloud.
Operations are held in memory: after a restart their names answer NOT_FOUND. A cluster whose provisioning a restart interrupted stays PROVISIONING and can be deleted.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: clusters CRUD
limitations: CreateCluster validates the name (1-40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens) and records the cluster as PROVISIONING, then returns an operation that becomes DONE when k3d provisioning ends, with the cluster RUNNING or in ERROR. Operations are read through projects.locations.operations.get/list (and the zonal operations routes); location - lists every location of the project. A duplicate create is ALREADY_EXISTS (409), a delete while the cluster is still provisioning is FAILED_PRECONDITION (400), a missing cluster is NOT_FOUND (404). Delete tears down the k3d cluster before it answers and returns a finished operation. GET returns the create request's fields with the cluster's status, endpoint, version, node count and CA certificate. UpdateCluster is not implemented.

operations.label: pod workload identity (workloadIdentityConfig.workloadPool, KSA to GSA mapping through the pod metadata relay)
limitations: Not implemented in this runtime. A workloadPool of {project}.svc.id.goog is accepted and returned on GET (any other value is INVALID_ARGUMENT), but clusters get no admission webhook or metadata relay, Kubernetes service-account annotations are not read, and pods receive no LocalCloud-minted credentials.

operations.label: node pools, autoscaling, upgrades
limitations: No node-pool RPC is implemented: every node-pool RPC answers UNIMPLEMENTED over gRPC and the REST nodePools paths are not served. Each cluster has one k3d node.

services.name: Compute Engine

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (instance records and common instance metadata); instance containers run on the host Docker daemon
persistence.restartBehavior: Instance records and metadata survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept; operations are memory-only.
recoveryLimitations: Instance containers have their own Docker lifecycle and are not reconciled at startup.

limitations: Compute Engine is not a supported LocalCloud service. A default-disabled local facade exists for applications that enable it explicitly.

The facade runs instances as Docker containers, not VMs. Every instance runs the ubuntu:22.04 container image whatever boot image it names, unless its metadata sets container-image; without a reachable Docker daemon an instance is recorded as a simulated VM. Startup scripts are never executed.

The facade serves, under /compute/v1, projects.get, projects.setCommonInstanceMetadata, instances insert, get, list, start, stop, delete and setMetadata, boot-disk reads (disks.get, disks.list), a static public image list (images.get, images.getFromFamily, images.list), zones.get, zone operations get, wait and list, and globalOperations.get. Other Compute paths are not served (404).

Metadata is stored with a fingerprint; a stale fingerprint answers 412. Start, stop, insert and metadata operations are kept in memory and answer 404 after a restart. No metadata server or workload identity is provided to instances.
Disks, snapshots, instance templates, machine types, networks and firewalls are not provided; VMs, hypervisor behaviour and Google networking run only in Google Cloud.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: instances.create/get/list/start/stop/delete
limitations: Not a supported LocalCloud capability. When explicitly enabled, the local facade runs each instance as a Docker container, answers instances.insert with a finished zonal operation, and refuses a duplicate name with 409.

operations.label: disks, snapshots, templates, networking
limitations: Not provided. The facade only reports each instance's boot disk through disks.get and disks.list.

services.name: Cloud Run

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (services, revisions and the shared operation records); revision containers run on the host Docker daemon
persistence.restartBehavior: Service and revision records survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept. A running container is adopted; a missing or stopped one leaves the service STOPPED until it is redeployed. Operations stay readable through google.longrunning.Operations; the REST operations route reads only operations started since the last start.
recoveryLimitations: Revision containers are Docker containers with their own lifecycle; the runtime does not relaunch them after a restart.
If the Docker daemon is unreachable, delete and reset keep the records and answer UNAVAILABLE until Docker answers again.

limitations: Cloud Run is opt-in and needs Docker access. Each revision runs as one always-on Docker container; template scaling, maxInstanceRequestConcurrency, executionEnvironment, serviceAccount, labels, annotations, VPC access and the other Service and template fields LocalCloud does not apply are stored and returned without effect. template.timeout sets the /run/invoke deadline only.

Applied to the container: image, a single container port (8080 by default), literal env values, command, args, workingDir, resources.limits cpu and memory, startupProbe (tcpSocket or httpGet on the container port) and healthCheckDisabled. The container also gets PORT, K_SERVICE and K_REVISION. A cpu limit below 10m, a memory limit below 6Mi, a malformed quantity or another limits key is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Refused with UNIMPLEMENTED (HTTP 501 on REST): volumes and volumeMounts, a second container, dependsOn, livenessProbe, readinessProbe, a probe of another port, a GPU limit, port name h2c, an ingress other than INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL, MANUAL scaling or manualInstanceCount, more than one traffic target or one that is not 100 percent to the latest revision, and Secret Manager env references (v2 env[].valueSource). On the Knative v1 API, env[].valueFrom and a non-all ingress annotation are 501 and an unknown spec field or traffic split is 400. A request carrying an etag is ABORTED because LocalCloud issues none.

CreateService needs a serviceId of 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise); the name is built from the parent and serviceId and a name in the body is ignored. Revisions are named {service}-{generation}; a template revision name is ignored.

Implemented: Services create, get, list, update (with update masks) and delete, and Revisions get and list over gRPC. Jobs (CreateJob, RunJob, GetJob, ListJobs, UpdateJob, DeleteJob) answer UNIMPLEMENTED; Executions, Tasks and worker pools are not served. DeleteRevision answers a finished operation and removes nothing. GetIamPolicy, SetIamPolicy and TestIamPermissions on services are stubs that store no policy.

Over REST, revisions are not served at /v2/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/services/{service}/revisions; use the gRPC Revisions API. The Knative v1 API serves service create, get, list and delete; replace (PUT) and Knative revision routes are not served.

Service.uri is http://localhost:{port}, a Docker-assigned port on the host loopback that belongs to the serving revision's container. It changes with every new revision and is empty while no container serves. Calls to the uri reach the container directly, without the gateway's IAM checks.

The gateway proxy /run/invoke/{location}/{project}/{service} (target path in ?path= or X-Target-Path) relays to the serving container. Request bodies are capped at 32 MiB (413 beyond), management request bodies at 4 MiB. It answers 504 past the revision's timeout (300 s by default, at most 3600 s), 502 when the container does not answer, 503 when no container serves and 404 for an unknown service. The control token and Console cookie are never forwarded.

A revision is READY once its startup probe passes: without a startupProbe a TCP connection to the container port, retried for up to 240 seconds; healthCheckDisabled skips it. A container that exits first fails the revision. A failed first deployment fails its operation and releases the name; a failed update records a FAILED revision, sets the Ready condition to CONDITION_FAILED with reason REVISION_FAILED, and the previous revision keeps serving.

After a gateway restart a service whose container still runs keeps serving at its uri. Containers are not relaunched: a service whose container is gone or stopped reports STOPPED and must be redeployed, and one whose container Docker cannot report on is UNAVAILABLE and checked again in the background. /browse/cloudrun reports runtimeState.

Containers carry the runtime's data-volume label; reset, delete and the startup sweep remove only containers of this LocalCloud volume. A delete or reset that cannot reach Docker answers UNAVAILABLE and keeps the service. Containers from builds before the label are never swept and must be removed with docker rm -fv.
Local domain mappings and revision traffic splitting are not implemented; Google Front End routing, managed TLS and autoscaling run only in Google Cloud.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: services/revisions
limitations: CreateService and UpdateService (gRPC, REST v2 and Knative v1) validate the request, return a long-running operation and deploy one Docker container per revision; poll through google.longrunning.Operations or REST GET /v2/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/operations/{operation}. A duplicate create is ALREADY_EXISTS. An update with an update mask changes only the named fields of the latest accepted spec; without a mask it replaces the service. Service reads report generation, observedGeneration, latestReadyRevision, uri and the Ready terminalCondition; GetRevision and ListRevisions (gRPC) return each revision's containers, scaling and generation. Delete removes the containers before the records and fences a deployment still running. Revision traffic splitting, Revision conditions and reconciling are not reported.

operations.label: jobs
limitations: Every Jobs RPC (create, run, get, list, update, delete) answers UNIMPLEMENTED; Executions and Tasks are not served.

operations.label: custom domains, production routing
limitations: No domain mappings or host and revision routing; services are reached at their localhost uri or through /run/invoke.

services.name: Memorystore (Redis/Valkey)

persistence.backingStore: Valkey append-only file under /var/lib/localcloud/redis-data, plus instance, retired-database, ACL policy and token user records in the bundled PostgreSQL
persistence.restartBehavior: Keys and instance records survive a restart with the LocalCloud volume (append_fsync everysec by default). A gateway restart leaves a running Valkey and its client connections up. Admin operations are kept in memory and are gone after a restart.
recoveryLimitations: Memorystore is not checkpointed; managed persistence modes, snapshots and failover are not emulated.
Retired logical databases are never reclaimed on the same data volume.

limitations: Data commands run on a real Valkey server, so Lua, Pub/Sub, streams and MULTI/EXEC behave natively. Every instance shares that server at 127.0.0.1:5390 (5394 with TLS when LocalCloud TLS is enabled). An instance is a logical database number, reported as redisDb in instance reads, which clients must SELECT.

Valkey has no password or ACL configured: AUTH strings, ACL policies and token users are stored and returned by the API but not enforced, and the ports accept clients without credentials wherever they are published. Logical database numbers isolate neither Pub/Sub channels nor SELECT, so any client can reach every instance's keys.

CONFIG, DEBUG, MODULE, SHUTDOWN, REPLICAOF and SLAVEOF are disabled on the engine. redisConfigs, tier, memorySizeGb and persistenceMode in instance requests are stored only; engine limits come from the memorystore settings max_memory, max_memory_policy, databases and append_fsync.

At most 16 logical databases can be allocated per LocalCloud data volume, across every project, and a create beyond that fails (409 or 500). A deleted instance's database is retired and never reused, even after a reset, so about 16 create and delete cycles exhaust the pool; a fresh data volume reclaims it.

The admin API (/v1 and /redis/v1 paths) serves instance create, get, list, patch and delete, upgrade, authString and operations; locations/- lists every location. PATCH changes displayName, labels and redisConfigs, and the maps named by updateMask replace the stored maps; upgrade changes only the recorded redisVersion. Other instance verbs, such as export, import and failover, answer 501 UNIMPLEMENTED. Operations are returned done.
Cluster resources, backup collections and backups are not emulated. The shared regional and cluster certificate authority endpoints return a placeholder certificate that clients cannot use.

Checkpoints refuse Memorystore (GLOBAL_SERVICE_NOT_CHECKPOINTABLE) and exports have no Memorystore section; a seed can create instances and keys. Deleting an instance flushes its database, and a global reset runs FLUSHALL and fails when Valkey refuses it or does not accept connections within 30 seconds.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: RESP commands
limitations: Native Valkey data commands, including Lua, Pub/Sub, streams and MULTI/EXEC. Server administration commands (CONFIG, DEBUG, MODULE, SHUTDOWN, REPLICAOF, SLAVEOF) are disabled, and logical databases share one unauthenticated server.

operations.label: Cloud Redis admin API
limitations: Instance create, get, list, patch, delete, upgrade, authString and operation reads under /v1 and /redis/v1. PATCH applies displayName, labels and redisConfigs as records; capacity, tier and version changes do not reach the engine, and other instance verbs answer 501. Cluster resources are not implemented.

services.name: Cloud Workflows

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (workflows, revisions, executions, step history, operations and environment variables)
persistence.restartBehavior: Workflows, revisions, finished executions, step history, operations and environment variables reload after a restart while the volume is kept. ACTIVE executions fail with InstanceRestart; QUEUED executions run from their first step once the gateway accepts requests.
recoveryLimitations: Steps an interrupted execution already ran are not undone, and their external side effects remain.

limitations: Workflow definitions, revisions, executions and step history persist. An execution that was ACTIVE when LocalCloud stopped is not resumed; it fails with InstanceRestart. A QUEUED execution has run no step and runs after the restart from its first step, with the workflow's current source and service account (not necessarily the revision it was created for), once the gateway accepts requests; it fails with InstanceRestart only when its workflow no longer exists.

A local interpreter implements Workflows syntax and a subset of the standard library and connectors. Workflows are validated at deploy, and a malformed one is refused at create or update (400) with the step named. Conditions in switch, if, and, or, not and retry predicates must be booleans: a number, string or missing field raises TypeError. Equality needs operands of one type, so 1 == "1" is false; integer overflow raises ValueError.

http.* calls raise HttpError for a 400 to 599 answer, with code, headers and body, and ConnectionFailedError, ConnectionError or TimeoutError for transport failures; connector failures carry the same tags, so handlers read e.code and e.body. http.* never follows redirects. Connectors apply none of Google's built-in retry policies, and local long-running operations finish at once, so polling options have no effect.

Connectors call LocalCloud's own services for these API families: Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Firestore, BigQuery, Secret Manager, Cloud Tasks, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, Workflows and Workflow Executions, Spanner, Cloud SQL Admin, AlloyDB, Bigtable Admin, Compute Engine, GKE, Dataproc, Logging, Cloud KMS and Vertex AI, each with a limited set of methods.

Limits: 100,000 steps per execution, shared by parallel branches and child workflows; call depth 20, then RecursionError; 2 to 10 branches per parallel step and nesting depth 2; 100 unhandled errors in parallel steps, then an uncatchable ResourceLimitError; values up to 8 MiB and lists or maps up to 10,000 entries (ResourceLimitError); source up to 128 KiB, execution argument up to 32 KiB, HTTP responses up to 2 MiB; sys.sleep up to 31,536,000 seconds.
At most 256 executions run at once and the rest wait QUEUED. Creating an execution beyond 4,096 queued or running answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (HTTP 429).

sys.get_env reads the workflow's environment variables and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID, GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION and GOOGLE_CLOUD_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ID; any other name returns null, and it takes no default argument. sys.log writes to the local Logging service, up to 1000 entries per execution.

events.await_callback returns a map with http_request (body, headers, method, query and url), received_time and type. An endpoint accepts the one http_callback_method (POST by default) and answers 405 to any other; it keeps one request that arrives before the await and answers 429 to another until that one is taken, and after its execution ends it answers 404. The default timeout is 43200 seconds and a timeout raises TimeoutError. Callback requests are not authorized in any IAM mode, and the callback URL names the gateway (http://localhost:5380 by default).

An execution runs as the workflow's serviceAccount, fixed when the execution is created; child executions use the child workflow's account. When serviceAccount is unset, LocalCloud uses default@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com, which exists only for the gateway's configured project unless you create it.

http.* auth OIDC and OAuth2 tokens are signed by the LocalCloud issuer as the execution account, for HTTP as well as HTTPS targets. A token that cannot be minted raises AuthError with IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE and sends nothing; an unknown auth.type raises ValueError. Cloud Storage and Cloud KMS connector calls are authorized as the execution account, Firestore connector calls need its access token (AuthError otherwise), and other connector calls carry its access token when one can be minted.

In strict mode, workflow create, update and delete and execution create need the workflow permission for the verified caller, a workflow with a serviceAccount also needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on that account, and anonymous calls are refused (403). A child execution is authorized for the parent's run-as account. Open and permissive modes do not check.

Finished executions, step history and workflow operations are kept by default; the workflows settings executions_keep_per_workflow and operations_keep limit them. Step history records variables only at history level DETAILED.
Seeds deploy workflows, and re-seeding an unchanged workflow changes nothing. Workflows are not included in GET /export or project checkpoints.

operations.label: workflow deploy/list/get/delete
limitations: Workflow create, get, list, update (new revision), delete and revision listing over REST and gRPC, returning long-running operations that are answerable after a restart. Definitions are validated at deploy and refused with 400 naming the step. REST bodies over 1 MiB answer 413 and non-JSON writes 415. In strict mode writes need the workflow permission and, for a serviceAccount, iam.serviceAccounts.actAs.

operations.label: executions
limitations: Execution create, get, list and cancel, with step history (exportData). The interpreter covers assign, call, switch, for, parallel (shared variables, exception_policy continueAll), try/retry/except, raise, jumps, subworkflows and child executions, callbacks, http.* with OIDC/OAuth2 auth, and standard-library modules including sys, text, list, map, math, json, base64, hash, time, uuid, retry and events. Connector coverage is limited to selected methods of LocalCloud's own services. Admission, resource limits and restart behaviour follow the limitations.

services.name: Vertex AI

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud (request log only)
persistence.restartBehavior: The request log survives a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept; model calls hold no other state.
recoveryLimitations: The request log grows without bound unless vertexai.request_log_keep_per_project is set.

limitations: Vertex AI is not a supported LocalCloud service. A default-disabled local facade returns deterministic stub responses for SDK wiring tests.

The facade serves only POST /v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/{model}:{verb} with generateContent, streamGenerateContent, embedContent, countTokens and computeTokens; another verb is 404 and a batchPredictionJobs create is 501. There is no gRPC service, no /v1beta1 path and no endpoint, tuned-model, predict or rawPredict route.

Responses are fixed: generated text repeats the model name and prompt with a short hash, an embedding is 16 values derived from a SHA-256 of the input, and token counts are whitespace-separated word counts. No model backend can be configured. streamGenerateContent returns one JSON array, not server-sent events.

Only text parts of contents (or content) are read; tools, systemInstruction, generationConfig and safetySettings are ignored. A body that is not valid JSON is answered as an empty prompt; bodies over 32 MiB answer 413.

Each call is recorded per project in a request log with bodies cut to 16 KiB. The database keeps every record unless vertexai.request_log_keep_per_project is set; reads return each project's newest 1000.
