operations.label: generateContent, streamGenerateContent, embedContent, countTokens
limitations: Not a supported LocalCloud capability. When explicitly enabled, the local facade answers these verbs with deterministic stub responses that do not reflect any model.

operations.label: models, tuning, batch prediction
limitations: Not provided; batchPredictionJobs create answers 501.

services.name: Cloud KMS

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud and state files under /var/lib/localcloud/kms (state.json for keys, versions, import jobs and policies; ekm-state.json for EKM connections); Autokey configs and key handles are database rows only
persistence.restartBehavior: Key rings, keys, versions with their key material, import jobs, policies, EKM connections and Autokey state survive a restart while the LocalCloud volume is kept; ciphertext from before the restart still decrypts.
recoveryLimitations: Each change writes the state file and then the database row, within a 10 second database timeout; a failed write is undone and answers UNAVAILABLE (503).
With server.persistence on and no database, Autokey changes are refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION.

Back up /var/lib/localcloud/kms and the KMS tables before upgrading; a refused state is recovered by restoring a readable backup or by clearing the state, which makes data encrypted under the cleared keys undecryptable.
Project checkpoints do not capture Cloud KMS; a checkpoint names the service as not captured.

limitations: Only SOFTWARE protection is local. Keys, import jobs and random bytes that ask for HSM, EXTERNAL, EXTERNAL_VPC or single-tenant HSM protection are refused with UNAVAILABLE (503), and LocationMetadata reports no HSM or EKM. Locations list global and us-central1; key rings are accepted under any location ID.

Automatic rotation and the end of a scheduled destruction do not run locally. rotationPeriod and nextRotationTime are stored and returned, but no new version is created when rotation is due; a destroyed version stays DESTROY_SCHEDULED (unusable and restorable) after its destroyTime passes. Only an import-only key with a zero destroy duration destroys at once.

Unreadable KMS, EKM or Autokey state is refused, not replaced: every KMS call answers FAILED_PRECONDITION and readiness reports KMS unhealthy with failure_code state_not_loaded until the gateway restarts with state this build reads. There is no in-product reset of a refused state. State written by an earlier preview build is not converted.

Key material, including imported keys, is stored unencrypted in the data volume and the database. The kms.root_key_file and kms.lifecycle_poll_interval_ms settings are accepted but not read, and root-key rotation changes no stored material.

Ciphertext uses a LocalCloud envelope format, so ciphertext produced by Google Cloud KMS does not decrypt locally and local ciphertext does not decrypt in Google Cloud. decrypt accepts only that envelope (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise).
Inventory, Autokey and protected-resource search cover project-scoped Secret Manager resources only; organization and folder scopes answer UNAVAILABLE.
Page tokens are signed per process and answer INVALID_ARGUMENT after a restart. Only the newest 1024 key-delete operations stay readable.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: locations.get/list and generateRandomBytes
limitations: locations.list returns global and us-central1 as software namespaces with paging. generateRandomBytes returns 8 to 1024 bytes with a CRC32C field; REST refuses an HSM or EXTERNAL protection level with UNAVAILABLE.

operations.label: key rings, CryptoKeys, CryptoKeyVersions, rotation, and primary-version lifecycle
limitations: Key rings, keys and versions support create, get, list (pageSize and pageToken, filters including create_time comparisons, totalSize) and update with update masks over gRPC and REST, with the same validation on both. Purpose and algorithm pairs, IDs, version numbers (32-bit) and destroy durations (24 hours to 120 days; 0 to 120 days for import-only keys) are checked. updatePrimaryVersion and manual rotation by creating a version work. Automatic rotation does not run: rotationPeriod and nextRotationTime are stored only.

operations.label: managed and raw symmetric cryptography
limitations: encrypt and decrypt with GOOGLE_SYMMETRIC_ENCRYPTION keys (AES-256-GCM in a LocalCloud envelope, with additional authenticated data), and rawEncrypt and rawDecrypt with AES-128 and AES-256 GCM, CBC and CTR keys, over gRPC and REST with CRC32C request and response fields. Disabled, destroyed and destroy-scheduled versions are refused; a non-base64 or truncated body is 400.

operations.label: asymmetric sign, decrypt, post-quantum signing, and public-key retrieval
limitations: asymmetricSign with RSA PSS and PKCS#1 (including raw PKCS#1), ECDSA P-256 and P-384, Ed25519, ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 (including external mu) and SLH-DSA SHA2-128s (pure and SHA-256 pre-hash); RSA and ECDSA keys sign only a digest of their own hash length. asymmetricDecrypt with RSA OAEP. getPublicKey returns PEM or raw public keys; a version with no public key is FAILED_PRECONDITION. EC_SIGN_SECP256K1_SHA256 is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

operations.label: MAC sign and verify
limitations: macSign and macVerify with HMAC SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 keys, with purpose, version-state and CRC32C checks, over gRPC and REST.

operations.label: ML-KEM/X-Wing decapsulation and enabled post-quantum signing
limitations: Keys with ML_KEM_768, ML_KEM_1024 and KEM_XWING are generated locally; decapsulate recovers the shared secret and getPublicKey returns the encapsulation key. Post-quantum signing is listed under crypto.asymmetric.

operations.label: version create/update, scheduled destruction, restoration, and due-destruction reconciliation
limitations: Versions can be created, enabled and disabled, scheduled for destruction and restored while DESTROY_SCHEDULED. A scheduled destruction does not complete on its own: the version stays DESTROY_SCHEDULED and unusable until it is restored. Only an import-only key with a zero destroy duration destroys a version at once.

operations.label: ImportJob create/get/list and RSA/PQ-HPKE wrapped key-version import
limitations: Import jobs with the RSA-OAEP 3072 and 4096 methods (SHA-1 and SHA-256, plain or with AES key wrap) support create, get and list with filters such as state=EXPIRED, expire after three days, and are served over gRPC and REST. importCryptoKeyVersion parses the key as its algorithm's family, requires an algorithm that suits the key's purpose, and a reimport must match the version's algorithm. Post-quantum import methods (ML-KEM and X-Wing) answer UNIMPLEMENTED (501 over REST) and create no job. HSM import jobs are refused with UNAVAILABLE; a duplicate job ID is 409 ALREADY_EXISTS.

operations.label: eligible key/version deletion, retired keys, and operations.get
limitations: A version can be deleted once DESTROYED, IMPORT_FAILED or GENERATION_FAILED (imported versions cannot), and a key once it has no versions; key deletion returns a completed operation and a retired resource readable through retiredResources.get and list. Because scheduled destructions do not complete locally, keys with generated versions normally cannot reach a deletable state. A REST DELETE of an empty key ring is a local extension that needs cloudkms.keyRings.delete, which only roles/localcloud.kmsSuperuser grants.

operations.label: KMS IAM policies, roles, conditions, testIamPermissions, and strict authorization
limitations: Key ring, key, import job and EKM connection policies are stored in the shared IAM policy store; getIamPolicy and setIamPolicy on a missing resource answer NOT_FOUND and store nothing, and testIamPermissions returns an empty list for it. In strict mode every KMS, Autokey and EKM RPC and REST verb checks its cloudkms.* permission on the resource, with inheritance and supported conditions, for the verified caller; an unmapped REST route is refused. A credential-less caller without the X-LocalCloud-User header is refused, and the local developer can create key rings on a new project. Open (the default) and permissive modes do not deny.

operations.label: structured KMS audit events and LocalCloud usage metrics
limitations: REST crypto calls (encrypt, decrypt, rawEncrypt, rawDecrypt, asymmetricSign, asymmetricDecrypt, macSign, macVerify, decapsulate) write a cloudkms.googleapis.com audit entry with method, outcome, status code and principal to the local runtime log. gRPC calls and administrative methods are not audited. Per-project request counts come from the gateway's general usage counters; Google audit export and quota telemetry are not provided.

operations.label: Secret Manager CMEK envelope encryption and lifecycle enforcement
limitations: Secret versions written under a customer-managed key store ciphertext, a data key wrapped by the local KMS key, and the exact key version. In strict and gcp-live the Secret Manager service agent (service-{projectNumber}@gcp-sa-secretmanager.iam.gserviceaccount.com) needs roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key for writes and reads; a disabled or destroyed key version refuses access.

operations.label: KMS Inventory key listing, protected-resource search, and summaries
limitations: KeyDashboard ListCryptoKeys lists a project's keys; SearchProtectedResources and GetProtectedResourcesSummary report Secret Manager secret versions protected by a key. The scope must be a project (organization and folder scopes answer UNAVAILABLE), and resourceTypes is an RE2 pattern matched in full against secretmanager.googleapis.com/SecretVersion, the only type reported.

operations.label: project Autokey config/effective config and Secret Manager KeyHandles
limitations: Project Autokey config get and update (honouring the update mask) and showEffectiveAutokeyConfig work; a project with no active config reports no key project, and folder-level configs answer UNAVAILABLE. KeyHandles support create (a completed operation), get and list with filters, only for secretmanager.googleapis.com/Secret; create provisions a SOFTWARE symmetric key in the autokey key ring with a one-year rotation period and grants the Secret Manager service agent on it. A duplicate keyHandleId is 409. Autokey state is kept only in the database.

operations.label: authenticated Workflows Cloud KMS connectors
limitations: googleapis.cloudkms.v1 connectors cover locations, key rings, keys, versions, encrypt and decrypt, raw and asymmetric operations, MAC, decapsulate, getPublicKey, import jobs and import, IAM policy methods, Autokey config and key handles. Each call runs as the workflow's service account, so strict-mode KMS checks and REST crypto audit entries apply to that principal.

operations.label: EkmConnections create/get/list/patch, EkmConfig get/update, verifyConnectivity
limitations: EKM connection and EKM config settings are stored, validated (a malformed parent or ID is INVALID_ARGUMENT) and returned over gRPC and REST, with strict-mode cloudkms.* checks. verifyConnectivity never contacts an external key manager: it checks that service resolvers are configured and fails only for the reserved test hostname invalid.ekm.test. Keys with EXTERNAL or EXTERNAL_VPC protection are refused, so no key uses a connection.

services.name: Cloud SQL

persistence.backingStore: Bundled PostgreSQL under /var/lib/localcloud/pgdata (PostgreSQL instance data and all Cloud SQL metadata) and the MySQL companion's data directory /var/lib/localcloud/mysql-data
persistence.restartBehavior: Instances, databases and their data, users, public certificate records, backup records and operations survive a restart with the LocalCloud volume; a recreated MySQL companion mounts the same data directory.
recoveryLimitations: Backups, restoreBackup, export and import do not copy database contents; keep your own dumps for recovery tests.
Project checkpoints and exports do not capture Cloud SQL.
The MySQL root password is stored under /var/lib/localcloud/secrets; losing it while keeping the MySQL data requires restoring the file or resetting the Cloud SQL MySQL data.

limitations: PostgreSQL instances use the bundled PostgreSQL 17 server on port 5391, the same server that holds LocalCloud's own metadata. MYSQL_* instances share one MySQL 8.4 server in a companion Docker container, on port 5406 by default (LOCALCLOUD_MYSQL_PORT sets another). Each Cloud SQL database and user is a scoped database and login role on the shared server; database and user reads report the wire names under their localcloud fields (physicalName, postgresPhysicalUser, mysqlPhysicalUser), and instance reads report the endpoints.
databaseVersion must be a POSTGRES_9_6 to POSTGRES_18 or MYSQL_5_6 to MYSQL_8_4 identifier (POSTGRES_15 when omitted). The label is recorded; it does not select an engine version.

settings.databaseFlags is checked against the six flags that flags.list returns (character_set_server, collation_server, default_transaction_isolation, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, lock_timeout, work_mem): any other flag, a flag of the other engine or an out-of-range value answers 400. Accepted flags are stored and returned but not applied to the engines. Tier, disk, IP, backup, maintenance and activation settings are descriptive. PATCH merges settings; PUT without databaseFlags clears them.

Instance reads report ipAddresses from settings.ipConfiguration as Cloud SQL assigns them (PRIMARY unless ipv4Enabled is false, PRIVATE when privateNetwork is set), every address 127.0.0.1. IP settings never change where the engines listen, and an instance with activationPolicy NEVER stays RUNNABLE.

New databases are created with the requested charset and collation; a MySQL charset or collation that is not a plain name, or one PostgreSQL refuses, answers 400. PostgreSQL encoding and collation cannot change in place (400); a MySQL database update changes the database defaults, not existing column encodings.

Creating an existing instance, database, user or client certificate common name answers 409, and a clone onto an existing name 409. Names containing '/' or control characters answer 400, and request bodies over 8 MiB answer 413. A failed engine step fails the request and leaves no record. If the stored Cloud SQL state cannot be read at startup, creates answer 503 until a restart.

When LocalCloud generates its own TLS material, serverCaCert on instances, connectSettings, listServerCas, listServerCertificates and sslCerts.insert describe the CA that signs the certificate PostgreSQL and MySQL present, so a driver can verify the server. With operator-provided certificates they describe the configured certificate, and with no TLS material they carry no certificate. Client certificates from sslCerts.insert and generateEphemeralCert are self-signed development material that the engines neither request nor check; the private key is returned once and never stored.

requireSsl and sslMode are stored but not enforced. sslCerts.delete removes the record without revocation, and resetSslConfig, addServerCa, rotateServerCa, addServerCertificate and rotateServerCertificate return a DONE operation without changing any certificate.

Every Cloud SQL operation is returned already DONE, because the work finishes before the request answers; a failure is the HTTP error of the request itself. The operations list keeps the newest 1000 (cloudsql.operation_retention_hours adds an age limit; 0, the default, sets none), and an operation dropped from the list can still be read by its ID.

instances.export, instances.import, instances.restoreBackup, promoteReplica, startReplica and stopReplica check that the instance exists and return a DONE operation without moving data. instances.restart restarts the shared MySQL server for a MySQL instance, which affects every MySQL instance, and does nothing for a PostgreSQL instance. Point-in-time restore returns a DONE operation without checking the source or creating a target. preCheckMajorVersionUpgrade returns no messages and getLatestRecoveryTime reports synthetic times.
backupRuns and the Backups API (projects/{project}/backups) store records in PostgreSQL and capture no database contents.

Project exports and checkpoints do not include Cloud SQL, so a checkpoint restore leaves Cloud SQL as it is. A seed can create instances, databases and users and run SQL; each seed statement runs once, as the instance's owner role.

MYSQL_* instances need Docker access: LocalCloud starts the companion (image agentcloud/mysql:8.4) on first use, or at boot with mysql_autostart. Its host ports bind to 127.0.0.1, plus the gateway's LAN address when the gateway is published there; its root password is generated per install and an empty one is refused. A containerised gateway started without the /var/lib/localcloud volume refuses to create MySQL instances. Cloud SQL declares no Docker dependency, so readiness does not report a missing Docker socket.

With mysql_enabled false, MySQL instances cannot be created, and deleting a MySQL-backed instance, database or user, or a reset that must drop MySQL data, answers 500 and keeps every record until MySQL is enabled again.
Cloud SQL user passwords are kept in plain text in the local metadata database.
Read replicas, high availability and failover, Private Service Connect, Microsoft Entra ID, SSRS leases, external server sync, blue-green deployments and managed maintenance are not emulated.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog; no service is gated by license tier.

operations.label: instances/databases/users
limitations: Instance, database and user create, get, list, update and delete through the Cloud SQL Admin REST API (v1 and v1beta4 paths), backed by real databases and login roles on the shared PostgreSQL and MySQL engines. Duplicates answer 409. Instance settings other than the database-flag check are descriptive.

operations.label: MySQL 8.4 data plane
limitations: One shared MySQL 8.4 server in a Docker container started on demand, on port 5406 by default and bound to 127.0.0.1. Each instance's schemas and users are isolated by name and grants, not by separate servers. Requires Docker access.

operations.label: instances.restoreBackup/preCheckMajorVersionUpgrade/export/import/resetSslConfig/listServerCas
limitations: listServerCas returns the CA the engines present when LocalCloud generates its TLS material. preCheckMajorVersionUpgrade returns an empty message list. export, import, restoreBackup and resetSslConfig check that the instance exists and return a DONE operation without doing the work.

operations.label: replicas and backups
limitations: Backups API (projects/{project}/backups) and backupRuns create, get, list, update and delete store records only. promoteReplica, startReplica and stopReplica return a DONE operation; no read replica is created.

operations.label: instances.clone
limitations: Copies every database and user of the source into a new instance on the same engine; copied users keep their passwords. PostgreSQL databases are copied whole and the clone is refused while the source has open sessions. MySQL copies base tables with their data and skips views. A missing source answers 404 and an existing target 409.

operations.label: instances.executeSql
limitations: Runs SQL against an instance database on PostgreSQL or MySQL. Results are capped at server.query_max_rows (10000 by default) and 32 MiB; a cut result sets partialResult, partialResultMode FAIL_PARTIAL_RESULT answers 400, and a failing statement reports its own error.

operations.label: sslCerts.insert/list/get/delete, connectSettings, generateEphemeralCert
limitations: Client certificate records hold public certificate data only; the private key is returned once by insert. Certificates are self-signed and not checked by the engines, and delete does not revoke. connectSettings returns the server CA when LocalCloud generates its TLS material.
